defect.summary: WebSocket endpoint has no authentication and no Origin validation, enabling cross-origin hijacking of a localhost agent that can execute shell commands.
defect.detail: The `WebSocketServer` is created without `verifyClient` and the `connection` handler accepts any socket, so a malicious web page the user visits can open `ws://127.0.0.1:18888/ws` (browsers do not apply same-origin policy to WebSockets, and 18888 is the hard-coded default port in address.ts). Once connected, that page can send `user_message` to start agent runs and reply `permission_response: "allow"` to its own `permission_request` broadcasts, approving Bash/PowerShell execution and yielding remote code execution as the user. Standard mitigation (rejecting connections whose `Origin` header is not the served host, or requiring a shared token) is absent. Review 2026-09-30: still no verifyClient/Origin/token validation anywhere in server.ts; parseRemoteAddress additionally permits binding any interface (e.g. 0.0.0.0), widening exposure beyond loopback when chosen.

defect.summary: tmux spawn embeds the shell-quoted command inside outer double quotes, re-activating $, backticks, " and \ in LLM-provided task text
defect.detail: spawnTeammate builds `tmux new-session ... "${cmd}"` where cmd's tokens were single-quoted by shellQuote. Inside the outer double quotes those single quotes are literal, so a task string containing `$(...)`, backticks, or `"` is interpreted by the leader's own shell during execSync — e.g. task text `x"; rm -rf ~; "` breaks out of the quoting entirely. The shellQuote JSDoc documents this caveat but the exposure remains: task text originates from model output and can execute arbitrary commands in the leader process. Review 2026-09-30: teammate name IS validated (teams/protocol.ts:43 /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/, tools.ts:153) but task text is not sanitized (teams/index.ts:355); the tmux branch embeds shellQuote output inside outer double quotes where $, backtick, " and \ stay shell-active. The iTerm branch is NOT affected: its single-quoted tokens reach the tab shell verbatim (no outer double-quote layer).

defect.summary: /rewind feedback and rebuilt transcript are never printed because Ink's Static only appends past its high-water mark
defect.detail: handleRewindAction replaces `messages` with a shorter rebuilt list, but the Static key (`transcript-${sessionId}-${termWidth}-${expanded}`) does not change on rewind. Ink's Static renders `items.slice(index)` where `index` is the previous `items.length` (verified in node_modules/ink/build/components/Static.js), so after the list shrinks, `slice` yields nothing and the "⟲ Rewound to checkpoint..." confirmation plus any rebuilt items below the old high-water mark are silently swallowed. The user gets no visible feedback that the rewind happened.

defect.summary: Concurrent prepare() calls with differing configs can reset SandboxManager under a running command
defect.detail: prepare() awaits any in-flight initializationPromise but then re-checks configKey and may call SandboxManager.reset()+initialize() while another wrapped command is still executing under the previous config. The comment in src/tools/bash.ts:257-262 explicitly acknowledges that "a changing allowWrite entry ... letting concurrent commands reset each other's sandbox state", confirming the race is real when configs differ; a command could run unsandboxed or against the wrong policy during the reset window. Review 2026-09-30: reset-on-config-change is deliberate; only the interactive TUI creates a sandbox, one instance per process with a stable per-session config (tools/bash.ts:257-262 deliberately keeps allowWrite stable), while remote/ACP/print wire no sandbox. Would become a live race only in a multi-session host using this backend. Second-pass 2026-09-30: obsolete — src/sandbox/sandbox-runtime.ts and the @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime backend were removed (commit 8a26f0d); src/sandbox now holds only index.ts/bwrap.ts/seatbelt.ts and zero sandbox-runtime references remain in src/. The recorded race and the bash.ts comment it quoted no longer exist.

defect.summary: rewind() deletes the live file when the backup read fails for ANY reason, not just a missing backup
defect.detail: The catch around readFileSync(backup.backupPath) treats every failure (EACCES, EIO, EMFILE, not only ENOENT) as "file didn't exist at snapshot time" and unlinks the current file. A transient read error on the backup therefore destroys user content instead of skipping it and leaving the entry for retry, which is exactly the resilience the baseline path (unresolvedBaselines) implements. Tests only cover the missing-backup case, so the broad catch is untested.

defect.summary: Busy-loop reader child process can be orphaned if the test fails mid-way
defect.detail: The spawned reader hot-loops on `existsSync(stopPath)` and is only terminated by the stop file written at line 354, after the 30-iteration persist loop. If `team.persist()` throws or the test otherwise aborts before the stop file is written, the child spins at 100% CPU indefinitely with no kill/teardown guard (no try/finally, no `reader.kill()` in a cleanup hook).

defect.summary: Plan-mode teammates are told every turn to call ExitPlanMode/AskUserQuestion, but both tools are stripped from teammate registries
defect.detail: The Agent loop injects buildPlanModeReminder whenever checker.mode === "plan", which holds for in-process plan-mode teammates (checker created in AgentTool.runAsTeammate, passed through spawnSubagent as checkerOverride). The reminder instructs the model to call ExitPlanMode for approval and AskUserQuestion for clarification, but cloneRegistryForTeammate strips both via MAIN_AGENT_ONLY_TOOLS, and the team layer documents that ending the turn is the plan-submission signal (teams/index.ts:459). The teammate receives per-turn instructions referencing tools it cannot call and may burn turns on "unknown tool" errors; buildTeammatePrompt ("plan approval ... handled by the host") directly contradicts the reminder.

defect.summary: Worktree-isolated plan-mode teammates write the plan under the worktree, but readPlanForReview reads a different file under the team workDir, so the Leader always sees an empty plan
defect.detail: The teammate's Agent sets checker.planFilePath = getOrCreatePlanPath(memberWorkDir) (agent/index.ts:345), which for worktree-isolated teammates is the worktree path, and the Layer-0 exception lets it write there. readPlanForReview then calls getOrCreatePlanPath(this.workDir) with the team's main workDir; because the plan path is a process-wide singleton with workDir-scoped lookup (plan-file/index.ts:41), the worktree plan fails isPlanUnderWorkDir and a fresh empty plan file is created and read, so approval proceeds with the "(Plan file is empty...)" fallback. The same singleton also flip-flops when multiple plan-mode agents with different workDirs run in one process, creating a new empty plan file on each switch.

defect.summary: Response body is fully buffered before the 10MB size cap is enforced
defect.detail: The content-length pre-check at line 251 only works when the server sends an honest Content-Length header; with chunked transfer encoding or a lying server, `response.arrayBuffer()` buffers the entire body into memory before the `body.byteLength > MAX_CONTENT_BYTES` check at line 276 runs. A malicious or compromised URL can therefore spike process memory far beyond the documented 10MB limit. The cap should be enforced incrementally while streaming the body.

defect.summary: No restriction on fetching internal/loopback/link-local addresses
defect.detail: WebFetch accepts any http/https URL, including localhost, private RFC1918 ranges, and link-local cloud-metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254, and follows redirects automatically. The tool is categorized "read", so it may run without a permission prompt, letting prompt-injected content steer the agent into probing or exfiltrating from internal services. Uncertain because this may be an accepted design decision for a local coding agent. Review 2026-09-30: consistent with the product trust model — the same agent exposes Bash/PowerShell/ReadFile under the same permission model, so a prompt-injected fetch of localhost/link-local grants no capability beyond local command execution; redirect following is openly documented in the tool description. Residual risk worth tracking, not an oversight.

defect.summary: Diff bodies are interpolated into <file> elements without escaping
defect.detail: buildConcatenatedDiffs escapes only the path attributes; the diff text itself is inserted raw. A changed file whose content contains a literal `</file>` or `<file path=...>` line (e.g. editing this very codebase, or any XML/markup file) can prematurely close or forge the element boundary in the review, plan, and filter prompts, corrupting what the model perceives as each file's diff. Review 2026-09-30: every d.diffText line comes from git unified-diff output with a mandatory +/-/space prefix, so a column-0 </file> boundary cue cannot appear in the interpolated text; the prompts are consumed as raw LLM text, not XML-parsed.

defect.summary: drainLeaderMailbox's failed-detection string never matches the in-process failure notification format
defect.detail: An in-process teammate that fails sends `[idle] <name> (reason: failed)` (index.ts:521), but drainLeaderMailbox tests `msg.text.includes(" failed:")`, which only matches the external format `[idle] <name> failed: ...` from teammate.ts. Consequently a failed in-process teammate's uiState.status is overwritten from "failed" back to "idle", and the `failed || stopped` branch is skipped so its name is never unregistered from the name registry — SendMessage to the dead teammate then vanishes silently.

defect.summary: Mutating team tools declare category "read", which the permission checker auto-allows without prompting
defect.detail: TeamCreateTool, SpawnTeammateTool, SendMessageTool, and TeamDeleteTool all set `category = "read"` (tools.ts:52, 108, 186, 407). PermissionChecker.modeDecide returns "allow" for category "read" in default and plan modes, so TeamDelete — which stops running members and recursively deletes the team directory — and process-spawning tools execute with no permission prompt. Comparable mutating tools (TaskStop, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate) correctly use "command".

defect.summary: cleanExpiredLogs scans ~/.yukino/teams/<entry>/logs but entries are namespace hashes, so teammate logs are never cleaned
defect.detail: Team data lives at ~/.yukino/teams/<sha256-namespace>/<slug>/ (team-file.ts teamsBaseDir), and teammate logs at .../<namespace>/<slug>/logs/. cleanExpiredLogs iterates the top-level teams directory and cleans <entry>/logs — one level too shallow — so expired teammate log files accumulate on disk forever. Found while verifying the (now corrected) comment in src/teammate.ts that claimed cleanExpiredLogs scans the sibling logs dir; the fix belongs in logger/index.ts.

defect.summary: Responses stream tracks function-call state in single slots, corrupting output if two calls interleave
defect.detail: OpenAIClient.stream uses single variables (currentToolName/currentToolId/jsonAccumulate) for function_call items, while computer calls use a Set and the compat client uses a Map keyed by index. If a gateway ever emits response.output_item.added for a second function_call before the first one's done event, the state is overwritten and tool_call_complete events carry mismatched ids/names/arguments. The official Responses API streams items sequentially, so this is defensive-gap rather than an observed failure. Review 2026-09-30: the official Responses API streams output items strictly sequentially (added -> deltas -> done per item), so the single-slot tool state cannot be corrupted by interleaving; the compat client uses a Map keyed by index because Chat Completions genuinely interleaves tool-call argument deltas.

defect.summary: snapshots.json is written non-atomically and without any lock
defect.detail: save() writes snapshots.json directly with writeFileSync (no tmp+rename, no cross-process lock). A crash mid-write leaves corrupt JSON, and load() then discards the entire snapshot/baseline history for the session. Two processes attached to the same session (e.g. TUI and remote) can also overwrite each other's state silently.

defect.summary: Legacy nextSnapshotSeq derivation can reuse still-live backup name suffixes
defect.detail: load() falls back to nextSnapshotSeq ?? snapshots.length for state files predating the counter. If such a legacy file was pruned in the past, live snapshots can already carry backup names (@sN with N >= snapshots.length) assigned before pruning, so new backups may overwrite still-live backup files — the exact corruption the monotonic counter was introduced to prevent.

defect.summary: MEMORY.md is rewritten without locking while background agents may edit it
defect.detail: writeIndex() (reached every turn via buildSystemReminder → loadAll, and via rebuildIndex after extraction) writes MEMORY.md with a plain writeFileSync, while the consolidation subagent can concurrently edit the same file through WriteFile/EditFile. Last writer wins, so index updates from either side can be silently lost. Review 2026-09-30 adds: buildSystemReminder -> loadAll -> writeIndex regenerates MEMORY.md from scanAllMemories on essentially every turn, so the consolidator's curated MEMORY.md is systematically overwritten even without a race.

defect.summary: Permission request promise left uncaught when the abort race wins
defect.detail: `Promise.race([permission, cancelled])` resolves with null on abort, but the `permission` promise from `context.client.request(...)` stays pending with no catch handler. If the client later rejects it (disconnect, transport failure), Node reports an unhandled rejection, which can crash the ACP process mid-session. Review 2026-09-30: Promise.race registers rejection reactions on both input promises, so a later rejection of `permission` after `cancelled` wins is swallowed by the already-settled race and cannot fire unhandledRejection.

defect.summary: Shutdown path drops the rejection rethrown by server.close()
defect.detail: `void server.close().finally(resolve)` — `close()` deliberately rethrows the first recorded error, and `.finally()` propagates it into a promise nothing handles. A failing close during SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown produces an unhandled rejection instead of a reported error.

defect.summary: InstallSkill fetches model-supplied URLs with no internal-address restriction
defect.detail: `fetch(source)` follows redirects and accepts any http(s) URL, so the model can probe loopback/link-local endpoints (e.g. cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254) and persist the response body into `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` where it can be read back. Permission gating on the "write" category is the only mitigation.

defect.summary: No Origin validation on the ACP WebSocket upgrade
defect.detail: The upgrade handler checks only the pathname; loopback-only binding is the sole access control. A web page open in the user's browser (or any local process) can connect to ws://127.0.0.1:18889/acp and drive the agent, including tool execution, unless the SDK's `createNodeWebSocketUpgradeHandler` performs its own origin checks. Second-pass 2026-09-30: severity raised medium->high for consistency with the remote-server missing-auth entry: same cross-site WebSocket hijacking profile (browser-initiated local connections are not stopped by loopback binding) driving an agent that executes tools.

defect.summary: Configured paths are interpolated into the seatbelt profile without escaping quotes or parentheses
defect.detail: buildProfile embeds allowWrite/denyWrite paths directly into `(allow file-write* (subpath "${variant}"))` strings. A path containing a double quote (e.g. a workDir or tmpdir with `"` in its name, or an attacker-influenced writable root) can terminate the string literal and inject arbitrary profile rules, potentially granting write access outside the intended sandbox or causing sandbox-exec to fail open/closed unpredictably. The bwrap backend passes paths via argv and is immune; only the seatbelt profile builder performs string interpolation. Review 2026-09-30: originally recorded as a high-severity sandbox escape; reclassified. The interpolation is genuinely unescaped (lines 87, 95-96 after comment cleanup) but not attacker-reachable: allowWrite/denyWrite derive only from host configuration (workDir, "/tmp", tmpdir() at ui/app.tsx:2104, plus the session output dir at tools/bash.ts:239-242), the model cannot influence them, and remote/ACP/print modes never create a sandbox. Triggering requires the user to launch yukino inside a quote-containing directory, and a malformed profile makes sandbox-exec fail closed. Genuine low-severity robustness/defense-in-depth defect, not a practical escape.

defect.summary: TeammateMessage component is exported but unused anywhere
defect.detail: Grep across src/ shows TeammateMessage and parseTeammateMessage are only referenced within teammate-message.tsx itself; teammate messages reach the conversation through drainLeaderMailbox's task-notification XML instead. The file's own comments acknowledge it is currently unused. Project policy (AGENTS.md) says dead code should be removed aggressively, but removal is a code change outside this task's scope.

defect.summary: reflowText splits overlong words by UTF-16 code units, not terminal columns or graphemes
defect.detail: In reflowText's overlong-word path, `word.substring(0, available)` and `column = chunk.length` count UTF-16 units while the width budget is in terminal columns. CJK characters (1 unit, 2 columns) can overflow the configured width by ~2x, and surrogate pairs/emoji may be split mid-grapheme. Downstream wrapToLines in renderMarkdown clamps the visible overflow, so impact is limited to reflowText's own width contract and possible broken characters.

defect.summary: Partial bracketed-paste markers are not exempt from the 25ms escape flush timer
defect.detail: The escape timer exempts pending input that starts with the OSC-11 or color-scheme prefixes, but not a partial PASTE_START ("\x1b[200~"). If the marker arrives split across chunks with a gap over 25ms (e.g. slow link), the pending partial bytes are flushed to Ink as literal input and the following "0~" is treated as text, desynchronizing paste mode. The comment at lines 83-86 only claims retention for reports, which matches the code.

defect.summary: Synchronous recursive filesystem walk runs during render for @-mention completion
defect.detail: scanWorkdirFiles performs a recursive readdirSync/statSync walk (up to 2000 entries) inside a useMemo during render whenever the @-mention cache is invalidated (30s TTL or fileFactsVersion bump). On large workspaces this blocks Ink's event loop for the duration of the walk, stalling input and animation; the 2000-entry cap bounds but does not eliminate the stall.

defect.summary: Feedback backspace deletes one UTF-16 code unit, splitting surrogate pairs
defect.detail: The plan-approval feedback field edits with `feedbackText.slice(0, -1)`, which deletes a single UTF-16 code unit. Emoji and other non-BMP characters are stored as surrogate pairs, so backspace leaves a lone surrogate that renders as a replacement character. This is inconsistent with the grapheme-aware editing used by TextField and InputBox.

defect.summary: Cursor movement and deletion in provider-login fields operate on single UTF-16 code units
defect.detail: Left/Right arrows, Backspace and Delete move `position` by ±1 code unit and slice accordingly, so with non-BMP characters (emoji) the cursor can land inside a surrogate pair and deletion can leave lone surrogates. Fields are mostly ASCII (URLs, keys, model ids), so real-world impact is low, but the Name field accepts arbitrary text.

defect.summary: Layer 3.5 sandbox auto-allow returns "allow" when Bash args.command is missing or non-string
defect.detail: If strArg(args, "command") yields "" (missing/non-string command), the subcommand list is empty, no deny/ask rule is evaluated, and the checker returns allow with reason "Sandbox auto-allow". This is mitigated in practice because the Bash tool schema requires a string command and Layer 1 evaluates the same empty content, but the layer itself silently approves a call it never actually inspected.

defect.summary: resolveRefInDir/resolveRef follow ref: symref chains without cycle detection or depth limit
defect.detail: A loose ref file whose content is `ref: <other>` recurses through resolveRef → resolveRefInDir indefinitely if the repository contains a symref cycle (corrupt or maliciously crafted .git data). isSafeRefName blocks traversal but not cycles, so the recursion ends only in a stack overflow, which may surface as an uncaught exception in callers like readWorktreeHeadSha. Review 2026-09-30 corrects the mechanism: each recursion level awaits readFile, so the stack unwinds — a symref cycle manifests as a never-settling promise (callers like readWorktreeHeadSha hang), not a stack overflow.

defect.summary: Mutating task tools declare category "read", so they skip write-permission checks
defect.detail: TaskCreateTool and TaskUpdateTool persist state to <workDir>/.yukino/tasks/*.json via TaskList mutations, yet all four task tools declare category = "read". The agent feeds tool.category into PermissionChecker.check (src/agent/index.ts:1048-1070), where "read" is auto-allowed in default and plan modes. Likely intentional for internal todo state, but it lets plan-mode sessions mutate persisted files without any prompt. Review 2026-09-30: all four task tools consistently declare category "read"; the task board is agent-internal bookkeeping persisted only under <workDir>/.yukino/tasks/, never user code, and the read category also drives concurrency batching (agent/index.ts:945-947). Prompting for todo updates would be noise; the plan-mode tension is accepted internal-state handling.

defect.summary: writeSpill swallows write failures that lack an errno code and returns the path as if written
defect.detail: The catch rethrows only when the error is an object with a `code` property other than EEXIST; a failure without `code` (or a non-object throw) is logged and treated as success, so the returned spill path may not exist. applyBudget/persistLargeResult then replace the in-memory content with a preview pointing at a missing file, and the full tool output is lost.

defect.summary: appendProjectRule does an unlocked read-modify-write of permissions.yaml
defect.detail: Two concurrent sessions or agents clicking "allow always" can both load the rule list, then each writeFileSync the full file, so the second write silently drops the first session's newly appended rule. Unlike the session store, no file lock (e.g. withFileSyncLock) guards this path.

defect.summary: compactPath hardcodes "/" and never compacts home-relative paths on Windows
defect.detail: compactPath checks path.startsWith(`${home}/`), but on Windows resolve()/homedir() produce backslash-separated paths, so the check never matches and paths are displayed in full instead of as ~/... The rest of the codebase (e.g. plan-file/index.ts:35-36) explicitly handles separator differences, making this an inconsistency rather than an intentional choice.

defect.summary: Gate-skip tests assert nothing beyond "does not throw"
defect.detail: "skips when memory dir does not exist" (line 89) and "skips when session gate not met" (line 128) call maybeRun() with no explicit expect(). The line-137 comment claims "the stub client is never used", but the test never verifies that (e.g. with a spy), so a regression that starts the LLM pass would still pass these tests as long as it does not throw.

defect.summary: Real-timer 100ms sleep used to wait for potential async work
defect.detail: The test sleeps 100ms with a real setTimeout before asserting triggered === false. If a regression ever schedules async work, 100ms is an arbitrary window that may be too short on a loaded machine, turning a deterministic gate check into a sleep race. A vi.waitFor-style poll or asserting on the lock state would be more robust. Review 2026-09-30: the 100 ms sleep cannot cause a spurious failure — `triggered` is only set if consolidation runs, and the 1-hour-old lock file deterministically blocks the 24-hour gate (DEFAULT_MIN_HOURS=24, memory/consolidation.ts:46) regardless of timing.

defect.summary: sleep(500) assumes partial output has flushed before stop
defect.detail: "preserves the captured output when a background task is stopped" waits a fixed 500ms for `printf partial-out` to reach the output file, then stops the task and asserts the output contains "partial-out". On a heavily loaded CI machine the child shell may not have flushed within the window, making the assertion intermittently fail.

defect.summary: sleep(300) before asserting a foreground task is registered
defect.detail: "backgrounds running foreground commands on demand (Ctrl+B path)" sleeps 300ms after starting execute() and then expects hasForegroundTasks() to be true. If process spawn is slower than 300ms the foreground registry is still empty and the test fails; the timing margin is wall-clock dependent. Review 2026-09-30: foreground registration is synchronous inside the startCommand promise executor (tools/bash.ts:574-578) with no awaits on the no-sandbox path, so hasForegroundTasks() is true within microtasks of execute() independent of spawn latency; sleep(300) is margin, not a race.

defect.summary: Abort driven by a real 20ms setTimeout
defect.detail: The interrupt test schedules controller.abort() with a real 20ms timer while the tool only resolves on the abort event. The test's correctness depends on wall-clock scheduling; under event-loop starvation the abort can land late, stretching the run toward the test timeout. Deterministic triggering (e.g. aborting after the tool_use event is observed) would remove the race.

defect.summary: WebSocket test port derived from PID can collide
defect.detail: `20_000 + (process.pid % 20_000)` picks a fixed port per process. If another process already binds that port, or two concurrent test processes have PIDs 20000 apart, startAcpWebSocketServer fails with EADDRINUSE. Binding port 0 (ephemeral) would eliminate the collision.

defect.summary: mkdtempSync temp dirs are never removed in several test files
defect.detail: at-expand.test.ts (lines 41, 51, 57, 64, 80, 99, 107), bash-background.test.ts (makeContext), bash-subagent-routing.test.ts (makeWorkDir), clipboard-image.test.ts (lines 58, 73), command-loader.test.ts (cmdDir), and consolidation.test.ts (makeTempDir) create temp directories that are never rmSync'd, leaking directories into the OS tmpdir on every run. Other tests in this set (acp-agent, build-guards, config) do clean up, so the pattern is inconsistent.

defect.summary: First ACP test does not dispose the implementation in finally
defect.detail: The first test's finally block only removes the workDir, while the two sibling tests also call `await implementation.dispose()`. The session is closed via session.close (which disposes the runtime), so this is mostly cosmetic, but the asymmetry means any connection-level resources registered by onConnect are only torn down when the client connection closes. Review 2026-09-30: the first test deliberately closes the session via agent.session.close and asserts dispose was called exactly once — that is the behavior under test; sibling tests call implementation.dispose() because they never close their sessions, and onConnect wires connection abort to implementation.dispose() (acp/agent.ts:541-549). Nothing leaks.

defect.summary: Truncation cap asserted as <500 lines while MAX_DIFF_LINES is 200
defect.detail: The "caps output for very large diffs" test asserts text.split("\n").length < 500, but src/tools/diff.ts caps at MAX_DIFF_LINES=200 (201 lines including the truncation notice). The bound would still pass if the cap silently regressed to anywhere under 499 lines, so it only weakly pins the documented limit; asserting against the exported/actual cap (e.g. <= 201) would catch drift.

defect.summary: Entire library-entry guard suite silently skips when dist/lib is absent
defect.detail: describe.skipIf(!existsSync(libEntry)) means that if the build stops emitting dist/lib (or the entry moves), all ui-only-dependency, @/-leak, and API-surface guards pass vacuously with no signal. The skip is presumably intentional for source-only checkouts, but a missing-artifact condition and a not-yet-built condition are indistinguishable here. Review 2026-09-30: describe.skipIf(!existsSync(libEntry)) is a deliberate guard so the suite runs on source-only checkouts; a completely missing build still fails loudly via the cli-entry hard assertion, so only the narrow "main.js built but dist/lib absent" case skips vacuously — an accepted trade-off.

defect.summary: Mocked-home temp directories are created per test and never removed
defect.detail: beforeEach points the mocked os.homedir() at a fresh mkdtempSync directory containing a written config.yaml, but no afterEach removes it, so every run leaks directories into the OS tmpdir. delegation-prompts.test.ts in the same batch shows the repo's cleanup pattern (rmSync in afterEach); this file omits it while writing real config files (mode 0600) to the leaked dirs.

defect.summary: makeCheckerWithTiers called with a temp-dir path as the user-rules YAML content
defect.detail: `makeCheckerWithTiers(makeTmpDir(), body)` passes a directory path string as `userRules`, which is written verbatim into the user-level permissions.yaml. It parses as a bare string (not a rule list), so loadRulesFile silently returns [], and an extra temp dir is created and leaked. The test still validates its claim via the project file, but the first argument was almost certainly meant to be empty/valid YAML.

defect.summary: makeChecker-based tests read the real ~/.yukino/permissions.yaml
defect.detail: makeChecker (and the "extra allowed roots"/"bypassPermissions" tests) construct PermissionChecker without redirecting HOME, so RuleEngine merges the developer's real user-level rules into every verdict. A user rule like `Bash(*) deny` would flip expected outcomes. makeCheckerWithTiers in the same file demonstrates the intended HOME-redirection isolation pattern.

defect.summary: No-op rewrite claim is not actually asserted
defect.detail: The comment says persisting the same default_provider index is a no-op with "no needless rewrite", but the test only re-reads the value (still 2). It never compares file content or mtime before/after the second persistDefaultProvider(2) call, so the no-rewrite behavior in src (provider-login.ts:230 early return) is unverified.

defect.summary: Real-timer sleep(700) race against a 1500ms command
defect.detail: "backgrounds running foreground commands on demand" waits a hardcoded 700ms of wall time before checking hasForegroundTasks() and backgrounding. The margin against the 1500ms Start-Sleep (plus pwsh startup overhead) is fixed and environment-dependent; a slow CI or a fast-completing/failed spawn could flip the assertions. All other timing in the suite is bounded by awaits on task.done.

defect.summary: Wall-clock bound on kill latency
defect.detail: "kills the process tree when a background task is stopped" asserts Date.now() - stopped < 3000. SIGKILL tree kills are fast, but this is a machine-load-dependent wall-clock assertion that can fail spuriously on heavily loaded runners without indicating a real regression. Review 2026-09-30: Date.now()-stopped < 3000 deliberately bounds kill latency (versus waiting out the 30 s Start-Sleep); the 3 s budget is ~100x typical SIGKILL tree-kill latency, so a failure would almost always indicate a real regression rather than load noise.

defect.summary: Identical assertion repeated
defect.detail: `expect(parseResumeArgument(["--resume"])).toBe(true)` appears at line 30 and again verbatim at line 35 within the same test. The second occurrence adds no coverage and looks like a leftover copy-paste.

defect.summary: Title promises timestamp coverage the test never asserts
defect.detail: "appends records with a timestamp" verifies entry content and append order, but never asserts the `[ISO timestamp]` prefix that record() writes (src/recover.ts:42). The timestamp behavior in the title is untested. Review 2026-09-30: uncertain resolved — "appends records with a timestamp" asserts entry content and append order but never asserts the [ISO timestamp] prefix that record() writes (src/recover.ts:42); the title's timestamp behavior is untested.

defect.summary: Temp dirs removed at end of test body instead of finally
defect.detail: The three "crash log" tests (lines 42-61, 65-78, 81-91) call rmSync only after their assertions; any assertion failure leaks the yukino-crash-* temp directory (afterEach only restores cwd). The child-process tests in the same file correctly use try/finally.

defect.summary: Real-time `wait(200)` sleeps used to await async teammate completion
defect.detail: The `wait` helper (used at lines 196, 215, 323, 428) races teammate task resolution against a fixed 200ms wall-clock sleep. Under loaded CI workers or watch-mode parallelism, mailbox notifications may not have landed within 200ms, producing intermittent failures unrelated to product behavior. Awaiting the member's `done` promise or polling the mailbox would be deterministic.

defect.summary: Narrow real-timer margins over 100ms theme-detection and 25ms escape timeouts
defect.detail: `await delay(120)` (line 115) and `await delay(40)` (line 150) wait on real timers with only 20ms/15ms of headroom over the src timeouts (terminal-theme.ts:143 default 100ms, terminal-input.ts:116 escape timer 25ms). A scheduling hiccup can make the assertions run before the timers fire. Fake timers would remove the race.

defect.summary: Wall-clock assertion `Date.now() - started < 1800` for prompt shell return
defect.detail: The test asserts the Bash call resolves in under 1800ms while a daemonized `sleep 2 &` grandchild runs. The assertion is inherently timing-based; on a heavily loaded machine, process startup plus the tool pipeline could exceed the bound even though the fd-mode behavior under test is correct.

defect.summary: afterEach assigns possibly-undefined values to process.env, coercing to the string "undefined"
defect.detail: `process.env.HOME = __origHome` when `__origHome` is undefined sets HOME to the literal string "undefined" (Node coerces env assignments), leaking a bogus home directory into every later test in the same worker. Sibling files (team-file.test.ts:57-66, teams-shared-task.test.ts:54-63) correctly `delete` the variable in that case; this file does not.

defect.summary: mkdtempSync temp directories are never removed in several test files
defect.detail: session.test.ts, teams.test.ts (`workDir()`), teams-shared-task.test.ts (`tempDir()`), todo.test.ts, tool-result.test.ts, tool-result-wiring.test.ts, tools-boundaries.test.ts (`makeContext()`), and skills.test.ts (frontmatter tests) create temp dirs with no rmSync in afterEach/afterAll, accumulating residue in the OS temp dir on every run. Other assigned files (search-tools, shell-background, skills2, teammate-mode, teams-concurrency, session-recovery-boundaries) do clean up, so the convention exists but is applied inconsistently.

defect.summary: `void mailbox.send(...)` followed by synchronous assertions relies on send's body being fully synchronous
defect.detail: The test fire-and-forgets the async `send` and immediately asserts the lock file is gone and `unreadCount()` is 1. This is only deterministic because FileMailbox.send (src/teams/file-mailbox.ts:140-157) performs its entire locked write before any await. If send ever gains a real await before the lock section, the test silently becomes a race instead of failing loudly.

defect.summary: Temp repositories created by initRepo are never removed
defect.detail: initRepo creates a mkdtempSync directory per test (two tests, each also spawning a worktree inside it), but the file has no afterEach cleanup, unlike worktree-safety.test.ts which tracks and rmSync's its temp dirs. Every run leaks two repo trees (with .git and worktree contents) into the OS tmpdir. Accumulates across local runs and CI.

defect.summary: No isolation from the machine's global git config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL / commit.gpgsign)
defect.detail: initRepo runs `git init` and `git commit` without setting GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and without `-c commit.gpgsign=false`, both of which worktree-safety.test.ts deliberately does. On machines whose global git config sets commit.gpgsign=true (no usable key) or an interfering core.hooksPath, the setup commit can fail or behave differently, making these tests environment-dependent while the sibling file is protected.

defect.summary: "cancels a scheduled stream flush when unmounted" only asserts clearTimeout was called at all
defect.detail: The test spies globalThis.clearTimeout and expects it to have been called during unmount, but any clearTimeout call from React/Ink internals during unmount would satisfy this — it does not verify the specific stream-flush timer was cancelled. The neighboring test at line 534 demonstrates the stronger pattern (advance timers and assert streamingText stays empty).

defect.summary: send()'s "handlers.length !== 2" guard is effectively dead because the useInput mock is never cleared
defect.detail: beforeEach never calls vi.mocked(useInput).mockClear(), so mock.calls accumulate across tests and slice(-2) always has length 2 after the first render; the guard can never fire again. If a future render pass registered fewer than two handlers (e.g. TextField unmounted while submitting), slice(-2) would silently dispatch to stale handlers from a previous test instead of failing loudly.

defect.summary: FORK_QUERY_SOURCE exists as two independent constants that must stay byte-identical for nested-fork detection to work
defect.detail: cloneRegistryForFork tags the cloned Agent tool with tool-filter.ts:181's exported FORK_QUERY_SOURCE, while runFork's primary nested-fork check compares against agent-tool.ts:63's private copy. If either string drifts, the primary check silently stops matching and detection degrades to the fallback history scan (which fails after compaction). agent-tool.ts already imports from tool-filter.js, so the exported constant could simply be imported.

defect.summary: Background fork runs bypass ASYNC_AGENT_ALLOWED_TOOLS, unlike background definition-based subagents
defect.detail: With run_in_background=true and no subagent_type, startBackground → runFork → forkHandler → spawnSubagent receives options.conversation, so the registry is the cloneRegistryForFork clone and options.background is never set; filterToolsForAgent's async whitelist is never applied. The background fork keeps tools denied to background definition agents (tagged Agent, TaskStop, team tools, InstallSkill), so the same run_in_background flag yields different tool policies depending on the routing path.

defect.summary: max_tokens escalation mutates the shared LLM client, leaking a raised output ceiling from a subagent into the parent and later runs
defect.detail: spawnSubagent reuses parentClient when a definition has no model/system-prompt override (spawn.ts:108), so a subagent that hits max_tokens calls setMaxOutputTokens on the parent's client. The parent Agent's own maxOutput field, which manageContext uses for context budgeting, is not updated, so the token-budget computation and the actual request ceiling diverge for all subsequent turns sharing that client.

defect.summary: Frontmatter end is located with indexOf("---", 3), which matches "---" anywhere, including inside YAML values
defect.detail: A definition whose frontmatter contains "---" inside a multi-line string (e.g. a description containing a horizontal rule or dashed text) truncates the YAML block at that position. The definition then either fails schema validation and is dropped with only an error log, or parses with wrong fields. A line-anchored delimiter match would be robust.

defect.summary: plan_mode_required is checked with strict === true while run_in_background uses boolArg, so a string "true" silently starts the teammate without plan mode
defect.detail: boolArg coerces truthy non-booleans (utils/index.ts:187), but args.plan_mode_required === true accepts only a real boolean. If the model sends plan_mode_required as the string "true", the teammate spawns in acceptEdits mode instead of plan mode, silently losing the read-only gating, with no error surfaced to the caller.

defect.summary: Mac helper exit-cleanup handler is never unregistered when compilation fails
defect.detail: `compileMacHelper` registers an exit-cleanup hook before running swiftc, but the catch path at line 997 only removes the temp directory without unregistering the hook — unlike the Windows counterpart (`compileWindowsHelper`, lines 1018/1049) which correctly calls `unregisterCleanup()`. Repeated compile failures (e.g. missing Xcode tools with retries) accumulate dead handlers in the exit-cleanup registry, each closing over a deleted directory path.

defect.summary: xdotool key names are passed without a `--` end-of-options separator
defect.detail: On Linux, `runXdotool(["key", keys.join("+")])` and the keydown/keyup loops (lines 1107, 1112) pass model-supplied key tokens directly; a token beginning with `-` (e.g. `--sync`, `--clearmodifiers`) would be parsed as an xdotool option rather than a keysym. The `type` action correctly uses `--` (line 1237) but `key`/`keydown`/`keyup` do not. Key names originate from model output, which can be influenced by prompt injection in read content. Uncertain because xdotool may reject or reinterpret such tokens harmlessly in the key subcommand.

defect.summary: `abort()` fires `stopAll()` promises with `void` and no `.catch`, risking unhandled rejections.
defect.detail: `void this.backgroundTaskManager.stopAll()` and `void this.teamManager.stopAll()` discard the promises without a catch handler. If either `stopAll` rejects (e.g. a teammate/shell teardown throws), Node emits an unhandled-rejection warning or, under stricter settings, terminates the process. The `stop()` path awaits these same calls inside try/catch, so the fire-and-forget path in `abort()` is the inconsistent one. Uncertain because the underlying `stopAll` implementations may already swallow errors internally. Review 2026-09-30: both stopAll implementations swallow errors internally — TaskManager.stopAll awaits Promise.allSettled (subagent/task-manager.ts:170-197) and TeamManager.stopAll wraps every team.stopAll() in Promise.allSettled (teams/index.ts:805-806). The only residual path is a synchronous throw from a cancel() callback, which abort/kill operations do not produce.

defect.summary: Client `streaming` flag is not reconciled on reconnect, so the UI can stay stuck in streaming mode.
defect.detail: On `onclose` the hook schedules a reconnect but never resets chat state, and the server's reconnect payload (`connected` + `status`) carries no run/streaming information. If the socket drops mid-run and the run finishes while disconnected, the client misses `loop_complete`/`error` and `state.streaming` remains `true`, permanently showing the Stop button and the steering placeholder. The `connected` reducer case in use-chat.ts also does not clear `streaming`.

defect.summary: `AgentHandleImpl.currentAgent` is never reset to null after a run completes.
defect.detail: The `run()` generator's `finally` clears `abortController` but leaves `currentAgent` pointing at the finished `Agent`, so the last agent instance (and anything it transitively retains) stays alive until the next run overwrites it. `takeSteeringLeftovers()` relies on this reference to drain the just-finished agent, so it is partly intentional, but the stale non-null reference between runs is a minor lifecycle imperfection rather than a clean teardown. Review 2026-09-30: currentAgent must outlive the run — handleUserMessage calls takeSteeringLeftovers() after the generator completes, which reads currentAgent?.drainSteering(); nulling it in finally would break leftover recovery. Retention is bounded (one reference, overwritten at the next run) and steer() gates on abortController. The field JSDoc was corrected during this audit to document the intentional retention.

defect.summary: Static-file containment uses `fullPath.startsWith(FE_DIST)` without a path-separator boundary.
defect.detail: The prefix check would also accept a sibling directory whose name shares the `FE_DIST` prefix (e.g. `.../dist-evil`). It is currently safe in practice because `ctx.path` always begins with `/`, so `join(FE_DIST, cleanPath)` always yields `FE_DIST/...`, but the guard itself is fragile; comparing against `FE_DIST + sep` (or using `path.relative` and rejecting `..`) would make the containment robust independent of that assumption. Review 2026-09-30: normalize() collapses interior .. segments and retains only leading ones, and the regex strips every leading ../ and ..\ sequence, so cleanPath can never begin with ../; a bare .. without separator resolves to the parent directory and fails the startsWith(FE_DIST) check.

defect.summary: `handleResume` skip guard `!msg.content` does not catch empty content-block arrays.
defect.detail: The comment states tool-result-only messages are skipped because they have no text, but `!msg.content` is only true for the empty string; an empty array `[]` is truthy, so such a message would fall through and broadcast a `replay_user`/`replay_assistant` with empty text (an empty bubble). In practice tool-result messages are persisted with `content: ""`, so this rarely triggers, but the `RestoredMessage.content` type (`string | Record[]`) permits the `[]` case (e.g. via compact `keep` messages), making the guard not fully aligned with its stated intent.

defect.summary: Chat `items` grow unbounded and the message list is not virtualized.
defect.detail: Every server event appends to `state.items` and `MessageList` renders the entire array via `items.map`, with `useAutoScroll` depending on the whole array. For very long-lived sessions this is an ever-growing render and memory cost with no windowing/recycling. Not a correctness bug, but a scalability concern for extended remote sessions.

defect.summary: Synthesized untracked-file diffs embed raw paths without git-style quoting
defect.detail: untrackedFileDiff/untrackedBinaryDiff interpolate relPath directly into `diff --git a/... b/...` headers and `+++ b/...` lines. Git quotes paths containing control characters, quotes, or backslashes, but the synthesizer does not, so an untracked file whose name contains a newline, `"`, `\`, or a ` b/` substring produces a diff that diff-parser's header regex mis-splits or fails to match, silently dropping or corrupting that file's review input.

defect.summary: Workspace fallback treats any `git diff HEAD` failure as "no commits yet"
defect.detail: tryGit returns null for every failure mode (corrupt repo, bad index, permission issues), not just the unborn-HEAD case the comment describes. Any such failure silently degrades to `git diff --staged`, which can yield a partial changeset that looks like a successful workspace review instead of surfacing the real git error. Review 2026-09-30: the fallback `git diff --staged` (via throwing runGit) shares the HEAD dependency, so genuine repo corruption also fails there and surfaces as an error rather than a silent partial review; the fallback only actually succeeds for the unborn-HEAD case the comment describes.

defect.summary: parseComments accepts entries without existing_code, contradicting its own error text
defect.detail: Only non-record entries and empty `content` are dropped; a missing `existing_code` yields an empty anchor that can never be positioned (resolution stays "unresolved"), yet the comment is recorded silently. The zero-valid-comments error message claims "every entry needs non-empty 'content' (and 'existing_code' to anchor a line)", which overstates what the parser enforces.

defect.summary: Split groups reuse the same label, producing duplicate group labels
defect.detail: enforceMaxFilesPerGroup and enforceGroupTokenBudget emit every chunk of a split group under the original `g.label`. Duplicate labels then appear in result.groups, progress messages ("[label] ..."), and ReviewComment.groupLabel, making groups indistinguishable for any consumer that assumes label uniqueness. Review 2026-09-30: chunks reuse g.label because they are the same semantic group split for size; no consumer requires label uniqueness (finalizeComments dedups by path:line:content), so duplicate labels are cosmetic only.

defect.summary: resolveComment treats a partially set line range as already resolved
defect.detail: The early return `cm.startLine > 0 || cm.endLine > 0` accepts a comment with only one bound set (e.g. endLine > 0, startLine = 0) without any matching, and relocateWithLlm would then mark resolution "llm" without verifying the corrected snippet. Currently unreachable because parseComments zeroes both fields, but the guard is fragile against future callers. Review 2026-09-30: parseComments zeroes both bounds as a pair and matchConsecutive sets both as a pair, so the "only one bound set" state the defect fears is unreachable — latent fragility against hypothetical future callers, not a current defect.

defect.summary: LLM re-location is skipped when the filed path is not in the changeset
defect.detail: In the resolve closure, `d` is looked up once from diffByPath before the cross-file probe; when the model files a comment against a path outside the changeset, `d` stays undefined and `if (!located && d)` skips relocateWithLlm even after relocateAcrossFiles fails. Such comments remain permanently unresolved with no LLM fallback attempt. Review 2026-09-30: relocateWithLlm requires a FileDiff to build its prompt; when the filed path is outside the changeset there is no diff to relocate against, so skipping the LLM step is necessary. relocateAcrossFiles already probed all in-memory diffs, and the main prompt forbids out-of-changeset comments anyway.

defect.summary: RELOCATION_USER wraps the diff in a ``` fence that diff content can close early
defect.detail: The template embeds `{{diff}}` inside a triple-backtick fence. Any diff touching Markdown or prompt files can contain a ``` line, which terminates the fence early and leaves the remainder of the diff (and the trailing instructions) outside the intended block, degrading the re-location call for exactly the files most likely to contain fences. Review 2026-09-30: same mitigation as format.ts — git prefixes every diff content line, so a column-0 ``` fence cue cannot appear in {{diff}}; the prompt is raw LLM text (only the response is parsed, via extractCodeBlock).

defect.summary: In-process teammate acks only typed shutdown requests; prefix-only "[shutdown]" notices get no shutdown_response
defect.detail: isShutdownRequest (protocol.ts) deliberately accepts plain-text messages starting with "[shutdown]" (manual mailbox writes, older processes), and stopOne itself sends exactly such an untyped notice to external members. But the in-process loop gates its acknowledgment on `req?.type === MSG_SHUTDOWN_REQUEST`, so an untyped shutdown ends the loop with no reply to the leader, breaking the request/response correlation the protocol documents.

defect.summary: External teammate drops already-consumed mailbox messages that follow a shutdown request in the same batch
defect.detail: receiveSync marks the entire batch as read; the polling loop then processes messages in order and `break polling` on a shutdown request discards any remaining messages in that batch permanently. Senders of those messages receive no error and no processing. Narrow window, but the messages are consumed and lost rather than requeued.

defect.summary: Restored external members are marked active/"running" without verifying the pane process still exists
defect.detail: hydrateMember sets `active = isActive && external` and builds a "running" uiState purely from the on-disk snapshot. If a tmux/iTerm teammate died while the leader was down, the restored UI shows it as running indefinitely; nothing probes the tmux session or process, and cancel (kill-session) on a dead session is silently ignored.

defect.summary: Synchronous lock waits (Atomics.wait) block the leader's entire event loop for up to 5s under cross-process contention
defect.detail: withFileSyncLock retries with sleepSync, which blocks the Node.js thread. All mailbox operations (send/receiveSync/unreadCount) and config/task writes in the leader UI process go through it, so a teammate process holding a lock — or a slow stale-entry cleanup — freezes the TUI until the lock is granted or LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MS (5s) elapses. Hold times are normally tiny, so this is a design trade-off rather than a likely hang. Review 2026-09-30: the whole lock/mailbox API is deliberately synchronous (receiveSync, unreadCount are called from sync UI paths) and hold times are single-file read/writes — a trade-off, not a likely hang.

defect.summary: External (tmux/iTerm) teammates ignore worktree isolation: spawnExternal always uses the team's workDir as cwd
defect.detail: agent-tool.ts computes a per-member worktree (memberWorkDir) and passes it only to the in-process runAgent factory and setMemberMeta; Team.spawnTeammate has no workDir parameter, so spawnExternal launches the process with `cwd: this.workDir`. The external teammate merely gets a prompt notice about the worktree path and starts in the main checkout, weakening the isolation guarantee for pane backends.

defect.summary: Stale lock entries are pruned only when the recorded PID is dead; PID reuse blocks cleanup until acquisition times out
defect.detail: liveLockEntries removes an entry only if it is older than LOCK_STALE_MS AND its embedded PID is not alive. If the crashed holder's PID was recycled by an unrelated live process, the orphaned choosing/ticket entry is never removed and every contender times out after 5s and throws, making the mailbox/task file permanently inaccessible until manual cleanup.

defect.summary: Leader crash between external spawn and the final persist loses paneId, leaving the member un-killable after restore
defect.detail: spawnExternal persists isActive=true before spawning, then spawns, then persists again to record paneId/cancel. A crash in between leaves the on-disk member active without a paneId; restoreTeammateCancel returns undefined, so the restored leader can only request shutdown via mailbox and cannot force-kill the tmux session.

defect.summary: Restored team mode is derived from the first member's backendType, so one in-process fallback permanently downgrades the team
defect.detail: TeamManager.get() computes `mode = tf.members.find(m => m.backendType)?.backendType`. Team mode is not persisted at team level; if the first spawn fell back to in-process (e.g. tmux transiently failed), every later restore treats the team as in-process even after the external backend becomes available, and new members spawn with the wrong backend.

defect.summary: Connection/abort SDK errors are classified as generic LLMError instead of NetworkError
defect.detail: OpenAI's APIConnectionError, APIConnectionTimeoutError, and APIUserAbortError all extend OpenAI.APIError with status undefined, so they pass the 413/401/429 checks and land in the generic branch, producing "OpenAI API error (undefined): ...". The NetworkError fallback is unreachable for these SDK-thrown transport failures, defeating the error taxonomy (and printing an "undefined" status to users). Second-pass 2026-09-30: re-verified against the current classifier (:1045-1080) — APIConnectionError/APIConnectionTimeoutError/APIUserAbortError extend OpenAI.APIError with status undefined and land in the generic branch (:1072-1074), producing "OpenAI API error (undefined): ..."; the NetworkError fallback stays unreachable for SDK-thrown transport errors. Impact bounded: the agent retry path branches only on ContextTooLongError/RateLimitError and the abort case is covered by the abortSignal check (agent/index.ts:511).

defect.summary: Connection/abort SDK errors are classified as generic LLMError instead of NetworkError
defect.detail: Anthropic's APIConnectionError, APIConnectionTimeoutError, and APIUserAbortError extend Anthropic.APIError with status undefined, so classifyAnthropicError returns LLMError("Anthropic API error (undefined): ...") rather than NetworkError. User aborts are mitigated because the agent loop checks abortSignal.aborted before inspecting the error, but genuine transport failures lose their NetworkError classification. Second-pass 2026-09-30: re-verified — classifyAnthropicError additionally lacks the `err instanceof LLMError` pass-through classifyOpenAIError has, so protocol-guard NetworkErrors and plain Errors thrown inside stream() are re-wrapped as NetworkError("Network error: ..."), mislabeling caller-side contract violations as network failures.

defect.summary: collectSummary rejects any stop reason other than end_turn/stop, including Anthropic's stop_sequence
defect.detail: If the summary response ends with stop_reason "stop_sequence" (or a compat gateway's equivalent), collectSummary throws "Compaction summary did not finish" even though a complete, usable summary text was produced. This turns a successful summarization into a compaction failure and increments the auto-compact circuit-breaker counter. Review 2026-09-30: the summary request configures no stop_sequences in any client, so Anthropic's stop_sequence stop reason cannot be produced; reachable stop reasons are handled correctly (end_turn = success, max_tokens = truncation failure, tool_use = caught earlier) and the "stop" allowance is vestigial. The defect premise cannot occur.

defect.summary: Bare catch collapses all discovery failures into a generic error, discarding the cause
defect.detail: The catch block in discoverModels swallows the original error (HTTP status, zod parse issues, network failures) and rethrows a generic "Model discovery failed" without a cause chain, making provider/model-picker discovery problems hard to diagnose. It may be intentional to avoid leaking endpoint details, but no logging preserves the cause either. Review 2026-09-30: the same generic "Model discovery failed" message is thrown consistently at four sites (current lines 100, 114, 119, 127), indicating deliberate detail suppression; the only downside is diagnosability, a minor trade-off.

defect.summary: Fallback config parse coerces flag fields with Boolean(), accepting non-boolean values
defect.detail: In loadSingleFile's degraded path (full schema parse failed), enable_coordinator_mode/enable_fork/enable_memory are read via Boolean(raw.x), so a mistyped value like the string "false" or a number silently becomes true instead of surfacing a config error. This only triggers when the primary AppConfigSchema parse already failed, so exposure is limited.

defect.summary: recordMetric hardcodes unit "ms" for every histogram
defect.detail: ProviderRuntime.recordMetric creates all histograms with { unit: "ms" } while the public API accepts any metric name/kind. All current histogram uses are durations, so nothing is wrong today, but any future non-time histogram (e.g. token counts) would silently be exported with an incorrect unit. Review 2026-09-30: all four histogram call sites (telemetry/instrumentation.ts:125,159,201,248) are durations in ms and every recordMetric caller lives in instrumentation.ts — the hardcoded unit is correct for the entire current API surface; the risk is latent.

defect.summary: prompt_history.jsonl is rewritten without a lock or atomic rename
defect.detail: append() does a read-modify-write of the whole history file with a bare writeFileSync: no withFileSyncLock (unlike the session module) and no tmp+rename. Two concurrent yukino processes in the same workDir can lose entries, and a crash mid-write truncates/corrupts the file. Impact is limited to prompt history, hence low severity.

defect.summary: extract() returns inconsistent name formats across the two save paths
defect.detail: The fast path returns basenames with the .md extension (memoryPaths.map(basename)) while the text-protocol fallback returns names without extensions. The TUI displays the list verbatim ("Memory saved: ..."), so users see "topic.md" or "topic" depending on which path saved the memory. Both callers currently tolerate it, but the return contract is incoherent.

defect.summary: Consolidation run failures are swallowed without logging
defect.detail: maybeRun() chains .catch(() => undefined) after the background run, discarding any error thrown by the consolidation subagent (including LLM and tool failures) with no log entry; only lock-release failures are logged. Failed passes are invisible in diagnostics and simply retry after the throttle window.

defect.summary: loadAll materializes .yukino/memory/ and an empty MEMORY.md with zero memories
defect.detail: buildSystemReminder calls loadAll(), which runs writeIndex() before the empty check; with no memories this mkdirs .yukino/memory and writes a newline-only MEMORY.md on every turn. That materializes the directory that MemoryConsolidator.maybeRun uses as its enablement gate, letting consolidation passes start on projects that never saved a memory.

defect.summary: Pending extraction runs inside finally and can mask the original error
defect.detail: In runExtraction(), if doExtract throws, the finally block awaits a queued runExtraction(pending). If that nested run also throws, it replaces the original exception; if it succeeds, its results are discarded because the original throw still propagates. The recursion-in-finally structure makes failure attribution and result aggregation unreliable.

defect.summary: No cap on the number of @refs or total inlined bytes
defect.detail: expandAtRefs/expandAtRefsWithImages bound each file (MAX_INLINE_BYTES) and the image count, but not the number of refs or the cumulative appendix size. A message containing many @tokens that resolve to files just under 100KB can produce an arbitrarily large outgoing message (cost/provider-limit blowup) with no total-size guard.

defect.summary: Reminder wrapper tags are not escaped against embedded content
defect.detail: addSystemReminder wraps arbitrary content in literal <system-reminder> tags without escaping. Reminder payloads quote externally influenced text (memory files, tool output, teammate mail), so content containing a closing tag can break out of the wrapper and forge reminder-level context for the model.

defect.summary: Fenced-code tracking toggles on any ``` line and can invert state
defect.detail: expandIncludes flips inCode on every line starting with ```, regardless of nesting or info strings. An unbalanced fence (also possible inside an @included file, where state is shared) inverts the flag, causing later @include lines to be wrongly expanded inside "code" or literal @ lines to be processed outside it. Review 2026-09-30 corrects one claim: inCode is a per-call local (line 157), reset on each recursion — it is NOT shared across @included files; the odd-fence-count inversion within a single file still stands.

defect.summary: Crash between tmp write and rename leaves orphaned rewind-tmp files
defect.detail: truncateSessionLines writes <file>.<pid>.rewind-tmp inside the sessions directory before renameSync. A crash in that window leaves the tmp file behind permanently: listSessions filters on .jsonl and cleanExpiredSessions only removes .jsonl files and per-session subdirectories, so nothing ever sweeps these orphans.

defect.summary: file-history directory layout is reconstructed inline despite a declared single source of truth
defect.detail: cleanExpiredSessions computes the file-history path as join(dirname(dir), "file-history", id) instead of calling fileHistoryDir(), which its JSDoc declares the single source of truth for that layout. Any future change to the layout must now be made in two modules or expired-session cleanup will sweep the wrong directory.

defect.summary: Connection-abort listener fires dispose() without catching rejection
defect.detail: `void implementation.dispose()` in the `onConnect` abort handler: if any `runtime.dispose()` leg (background tasks, teams, MCP disconnect) rejects, the promise rejects unobserved. Unlike `closeSession`, this path has no error channel. Review 2026-09-30: every dispose() leg is internally guarded — TaskManager.stopAll and TeamManager.stopAll use Promise.allSettled, MCPManager.disconnectAll catches close errors (mcp/client.ts:319-323), and runtime.abort() is null-safe (remote/server.ts:511-515) — so dispose() cannot realistically reject.

defect.summary: Downloaded SKILL.md content is buffered with no size limit
defect.detail: `await resp.text()` reads the entire response into memory regardless of length. A malicious or misconfigured URL serving a huge body can exhaust memory; the 30s timeout bounds but does not cap the download.

defect.summary: Frontmatter terminator matched by substring, not line-anchored
defect.detail: `raw.indexOf("---", 3)` finds the first `---` anywhere, including mid-line inside a YAML value (e.g. `description: a---b`), truncating frontmatter and corrupting the body. `parseSkillFile` in src/skills/catalog.ts uses a line-anchored regex for the same job, so the two loaders disagree on edge-case inputs.

defect.summary: walkDir follows symlinked directories and can recurse indefinitely
defect.detail: `statSync` resolves symlinks, so a symlink under `.yukino/commands` pointing at an ancestor directory creates unbounded recursion (stack overflow) at command-load time. No depth limit or cycle detection exists.

defect.summary: buildMcpToolName is not injective for names containing double underscores
defect.detail: Server `a__b` with tool `c` and server `a` with tool `b__c` both compose to `mcp__a__b__c`; the later registration silently shadows the earlier one in the registry. Sanitization maps hyphens to underscores, widening the set of names that can collide.

defect.summary: PromptResponse.usage reports session-cumulative totals on every prompt
defect.detail: `session.usage` accumulates via `addUsage` across all prompts and is returned whole in each PromptResponse. If the ACP spec intends per-prompt usage, clients that sum responses double-count; if it intends cumulative usage, the field name and per-turn return are still easy to misread.

defect.summary: disconnect() nulls the transport without closing it when client.close() throws
defect.detail: The catch around `client.close()` logs and proceeds to set `transport = null`, dropping the only reference. If close() failed before tearing down the transport, a spawned stdio child process or open HTTP/SSE connection can outlive the client.

defect.summary: Image conversion failures are always reported as "too large"
defect.detail: `maybeResizeAndDownsampleImage` can also fail on corrupt or undecodable base64 data, but the log message and the note injected into the tool output both assert the image was "too large to fit the API limit", misleading the model and the user about the actual cause. Review 2026-09-30: maybeResizeAndDownsampleImage throws only ImageTooLargeError, and only for an empty buffer or images >3.75 MB (images/index.ts:195-216); buffers <=3.75 MB pass through without decoding, and Buffer.from(base64) never throws — the "too large" wording matches every realistic failure mode except the 0-byte edge case.

defect.summary: ACP mode returns before initializeTelemetry(), so --acp/--acp-ws sessions are never traced
defect.detail: main() dispatches --acp/--acp-ws to runAcp() before calling initializeTelemetry(); teammate, print, remote, and terminal modes all initialize it. Users who configure OpenTelemetry/Langfuse via environment variables get tracing in every mode except ACP, with no indication that ACP is excluded. May be intentional, but nothing documents the exclusion.

defect.summary: -p rejects any prompt that starts with "-" and the error message suggests a fix that does not work
defect.detail: parsePrintFlags treats a following argument starting with "-" as a missing prompt and exits with "quote multi-word prompts", but quoting does not help: `yukino -p "-1"` is still rejected because the check runs on the raw argv token. Legitimate prompts beginning with a dash cannot be passed to print mode.

defect.summary: --remote is silently ignored when combined with -p or teammate flags
defect.detail: main() parses --remote into remoteAddr first, but the print-mode and teammate branches run before the remote branch and return, so `yukino --remote -p "x"` executes print mode with no warning that --remote was discarded. Flag-combination conflicts are otherwise rejected explicitly (e.g. --acp vs --acp-ws).

defect.summary: Malformed config.yaml degrades to empty defaults; the YAML error is only logged, not surfaced
defect.detail: loadSingleFile logs "invalid yaml" and returns { default_provider: 0, providers: [], ... } when yaml.load fails. The user then sees a downstream ConfigError about missing providers instead of the actual parse problem, which is only visible in the pino log file. A hand-edited config with a syntax error therefore produces a misleading failure message. Review 2026-09-30 corrects the mechanism: yaml.load is NOT wrapped in try/catch — a syntax error throws and propagates to main.tsx's catch, which prints it. The silent degrade applies when the YAML parses to a non-record (scalar/array/null): it logs "invalid yaml" and returns empty defaults, so the user sees the misleading "At least one provider MUST be configured" instead.

defect.summary: Command lookup is case-sensitive: /help Help and /Help report "Unknown command"
defect.detail: CommandRegistry.find uses exact Map lookup and parse() preserves the input case, so any non-lowercase command name fails even though all registered names are lowercase. CommandRegistry.complete() lowercases for completion, making dispatch and completion disagree. Minor UX inconsistency; many CLIs are case-sensitive by design, hence uncertain.

defect.summary: On a max_tokens stop, complete tool calls accumulated during streaming are dropped instead of being executed or persisted.
defect.detail: In the max_tokens escalation branch (633) and the recovery branch (664), the assistant turn is persisted with addAssistantFull(fullText, thinkingBlocks, []) — an empty toolUses array. If the model emitted complete tool calls (each tool_call_complete populates toolUses and yields a tool_use event) and then hit the output ceiling while generating further content, those calls are silently discarded: neither executed (the tool-execution path at 718 is skipped via continue) nor persisted, and no tool_result events follow the already-emitted tool_use events. The "Resume directly from where you stopped" message gives no signal that calls were dropped, so the model may proceed as if they took effect (lost work) or re-emit them (duplicate tool_use events). The block's comments address only the zero-text/zero-thinking cases, suggesting the case was unconsidered; rare because models normally stop with a tool_use/tool_calls reason after emitting calls. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — the escalation (:600-638) and recovery (:639-668) branches persist addAssistantFull(..., []) and continue before executeTools; completed tool calls are dropped, neither persisted nor executed, with no tool_result pairing the already-emitted tool_use events. Reachable on all three protocols (Anthropic max_tokens with completed tool_use blocks; compat finish_reason "length" with toolCalls; Responses max_output_tokens).

defect.summary: `send` silently drops outbound messages when the socket is not OPEN, losing user input and permanently desyncing permission responses during reconnect windows.
defect.detail: The send callback (144-149) checks ws?.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN and silently discards the message otherwise — no queue, no error, no retry. InputArea stays fully enabled while connection is "connecting"/"reconnecting" (app.tsx passes no connection state to it), so a message typed during the 3-second reconnect gap is cleared from the textarea (input-area.tsx:140-141) and never delivered. Worse, handleRespondPermission (app.tsx:77-87) dispatches respondPermission locally before calling send: if the frame is dropped, the UI shows "✓ Permission: allow" with the buttons removed while the server's pendingPermissions resolver (server.ts:1196-1204) is never invoked, leaving the agent run hung with no way to re-answer from that client.

defect.summary: makeContext() creates a fresh temp dir per test that is never removed, leaking up to ~10 MB of shell output files per run
defect.detail: makeContext (53-58) mkdtemps for every test; nothing deletes the directories; the file has no afterEach. "marks output that crosses the shell byte boundary" (291) runs node writing "あ".repeat(4000000), captured to a shell-*.output file up to the 10 MB truncation limit; several other tests add shell output and spill files. Each full run leaves well over 10 MB in the OS tmpdir, accumulating across local runs and CI. Same pattern as the recorded worktree.test.ts defect but with much larger per-run residue.

defect.summary: boolArg coerces any non-boolean value with Boolean(), so the string "false" (or "0") is treated as true
defect.detail: boolArg returns `fallback ?? Boolean(v)` when the value is not a boolean; all four call sites omit the fallback (bash.ts:216 and powershell.ts:182 for run_in_background, edit-file.ts:93 for replace_all, subagent/agent-tool.ts:279). Since Boolean("false") === true, a model passing the string "false" silently enables the flag — e.g. replace_all would replace every occurrence instead of one. The codebase itself documents that models emit wrong JSON types (coerceBySchema in mcp-call.ts exists solely to repair them), so schema-violating string booleans are a realistic trigger. Low severity because schema-enforcing providers usually reject non-boolean values before they reach the tool.

defect.summary: TaskUpdate with status "deleted" reports success even when the task does not exist
defect.detail: The delete branch calls this.list.delete(taskId) but ignores its boolean return and unconditionally replies `Task #${taskId} deleted` with isError:false. TaskList.delete (todo/index.ts:111-117) returns false for an unknown id, and every other path in the same tool correctly returns "Task not found" with isError:true (line 259). The model receives a false confirmation when deleting a nonexistent or already-deleted task.

defect.summary: TaskStore.save writes tasks.json in place; a crash mid-write corrupts it and load() then silently returns []
defect.detail: save() calls writeFileSync directly on the live file with no temp+rename, unlike the deliberately atomic writeConfigAtomic in config/provider-login.ts:104-120. If the process dies mid-write (recover.ts exists precisely because crashes happen), the JSON is truncated; load() (store.ts:62-70) catches the parse error, logs it, and returns [], so the resumed session silently loses its entire task board. Whether this warrants atomicity is a design call, hence uncertain. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — every comparable store in the repo writes tmp-then-rename (config/provider-login.ts writeConfigAtomic, teams/file-mailbox.ts, teams/shared-task.ts, teams/team-file.ts); tasks.json is the only in-place writer, and load() discards the board to [] on parse failure.

defect.summary: jq exit-code hint maps 5 to "no valid result was produced", but per the jq manual that outcome is exit code 4 (with -e) and 5 is the halt_error default.
defect.detail: The jq entry maps [2, "usage or system error"], [3, "jq program failed to compile"], [5, "no valid result was produced"]. The jq 1.8 manual states jq exits 2 for usage/system error, 3 for compile error, and with -e exits 1 if the last output was false/null or 4 if no valid result was ever produced; halt_error's default exit_code is 5. Codes 2 and 3 are correct, but "no valid result" belongs to code 4 and code 5 should describe halt_error. An LLM receiving jq exit 4 gets no hint; exit 5 gets a wrong one. The comment claim "codes per its manual" was removed during this audit; the mapping itself is code and was not modified.

defect.summary: Cancelling the question dialog is reported to the model as a successful answer with an empty answer list.
defect.detail: When the user presses Esc, AskUserDialog calls onComplete({}) (ui/ask-user-dialog.tsx:326-328), and the interrupt path also resolves {} (ui/interrupt-scope.ts:71). execute() then builds parts = [] and returns isError:false with output "User has answered your questions: . You can now continue with the user's answers" — asserting answers exist when the user declined, with no way for the model to distinguish cancellation from answering. Uncertain because resolving with an empty record may be deliberate to keep the agent loop moving; if so, the success wording should still reflect that no answers were given. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — every empty-answer path originates from cancellation (dialog Esc, the Cancel row, Ctrl+C interrupt via interrupt-scope.ts:71), never from an answer; the dialog's explicit Submit/Cancel distinction shows {} means the user declined, so the success wording is factually wrong, not an accepted design.

defect.summary: Backspace/Delete never resets dropdownIndex, so a shrunk completion list leaves a stale out-of-range selection
defect.detail: The character-insert branch resets the selection (setDropdownIndex(0) at line 891), but the backspace/delete branch (726-767) edits text and returns without touching dropdownIndex. After deletions shrink filteredCmds/filteredFiles below the old index, the dropdown still renders with no highlighted row, and Enter falls through to message submission because filteredFiles[dropdownIndex] is undefined (line 619) and dropdownIndex < filteredCmds.length is false (line 626). Up/Down recover via modulo wrap (line 776), confirming the index is meant to stay in range.

defect.summary: Partial OSC-11/color-scheme report prefixes are flushed as literal input by the 25 ms escape timer
defect.detail: Shares the root cause with the recorded PASTE_START defect but is a distinct manifestation: a buffer that is a strict prefix of a report constant (e.g. "\x1b]1" or "\x1b[?99") is retained by the prefix loop (line 74) yet fails the startsWith exemptions (lines 90-91), so the timer pushes it to Ink as keystrokes; the report remainder then arrives as ordinary text. Consequences: garbage key events reach Ink and detectTerminalTheme (terminal-theme.ts:173-183) never sees the terminal-response, silently falling back to "dark". Requires a chunk split within the first bytes of a report plus a >25 ms gap; rare on fast local links.

defect.summary: cursorWindow slices by UTF-16 code unit, splitting astral characters at the caret
