defect.detail: current = value[position] takes a single code unit, so an astral character at the caret yields a lone surrogate falling back to the " " placeholder (67-70), and right = value.slice(position + 1) (line 73) begins with the orphaned trailing surrogate, corrupting visibleWidth measurement and rendering of the after segment. The only consumer is provider-login.tsx:161 (cursorValue), where fields are usually ASCII and api_key is masked with BMP "•" — display-only and rare, hence uncertain. Unlike layoutInputRows/inputBoundary, cursorWindow has no grapheme-aware handling. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — the sole consumer (provider-login.tsx:161 cursorValue) moves the caret by ±1 UTF-16 code unit, so astral characters at the caret split into lone surrogates in the rendered output and in string-width measurement; grapheme-aware editing exists elsewhere (inputBoundary), so the gap is not design. Display-only, hence low.

defect.summary: initClient gates the initial MCP connection on the `mcpServers` prop instead of `mcpServersRef.current`, contradicting the ref's documented invariant.
defect.detail: The comment at app.tsx:344-346 states /mcp reload replaces the ref and "consumers must read this ref, not the prop"; connectMcpServers/reloadMcpServers obey this. However initClient checks `if (mcpServers.length > 0)` using the original prop before creating the MCPManager and calling connectMcpServers. If initClient (re)runs after a /mcp reload — e.g. a retry after failed initialization — it connects the stale prop list instead of the freshly reloaded config. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively as a false positive — initClient runs at most once per process (single call site gated on !clientRef.current, and clientRef is never reset to null); /mcp reload cannot execute before that because every submission path is gated by turnBlocked, which includes !clientRef.current. Prop and ref are therefore identical at the gate read.

defect.summary: The reducer's `goto` action is declared and handled but never dispatched anywhere.
defect.detail: The Action union includes { type: "goto"; index: number } (line 54) and the reducer handles it (70-71), but no dispatch({ type: "goto" ... }) call site exists in the file. The reducer is local to this file, so the action is unreachable dead code.

defect.summary: runUserTurn appends @-ref-expanded text to the live conversation but persists the raw text to the session log, so resumed sessions lose inlined file content.
defect.detail: expandAtRefsWithImages returns the original text plus an appendix of inlined @-referenced file contents. runUserTurn passes the expanded result to conversationRef.current.addUserMessage but saves the original text (or text + image blocks) via sessionMod.saveMessage. After /resume, rebuildFromSession replays only persisted records, so the model no longer sees the inlined appendix it saw live. May be intentional (persist raw user input), hence uncertain. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively; severity raised low->medium — runUserTurn sends the expanded @-ref text to the live conversation but persists only the raw text (plus image blocks); nothing re-expands on /resume, so resumed sessions permanently lose inlined file content the model acted on. No comment documents the asymmetry as an intentional tradeoff.

defect.summary: subagentCardsRef accumulates one entry per Agent tool call and is only cleared by /clear.
defect.detail: trackSubagent's finalize path calls subagentCardsRef.current.set(toolCallId, ...) for every tracked subagent run; no code path removes individual entries — only /clear calls subagentCardsRef.current.clear(). Long sessions with many Agent calls grow the map without bound. Entries are small (status + progress string), so impact is minor. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — entries are added by trackSubagent.finalize, read once at tool_result commit (use-agent-output.ts:192-195), and never deleted; only /clear empties the map. Growth is unbounded but each entry is tiny.

defect.summary: contextWindowRef and maxOutputRef are initialized from providers[0] even when defaultProvider selects a different provider.
defect.detail: The initial state of selectedProvider uses initialProviders[defaultProvider] (line 214), but contextWindowRef and maxOutputRef (293-299) initialize from providers[0]. When defaultProvider > 0, the Footer reads contextWindowRef.current and displays the wrong context window until the first initClient run corrects both refs — a brief incorrect display on startup. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — contextWindowRef/maxOutputRef initialize from providers[0] while selectedProvider honors default_provider; every functional reader runs after initClient overwrites both refs, so the only observable effect is a transient wrong context-window value in the Footer until init completes.

defect.summary: buildCommandContext hardcodes `permissionMode: () => "default"`, so remote /status always reports "Mode: default" regardless of the actual mode.
defect.detail: The /status handler renders ctx.permissionMode() directly as the current mode, and CommandContext documented the callback as "Returns the current permission mode" (that JSDoc was removed as a restatement during the pass-2 comment audit). The remote server supplies a constant "default" even though the real value handle.permissionMode is in scope two lines above in the same function and is tracked live (plan mode, bypassPermissions after plan approval). A user in plan mode or YOLO mode who runs /status gets factually wrong output; the terminal UI passes the real mode.

defect.summary: A plan approval that arrives while another run is streaming flips the permission mode but silently drops the plan execution.
defect.detail: planApprovalPending is set when a plan-mode run ends with ExitPlanMode success and is only cleared by cancelActiveRun or handlePlanApprovalResponse itself — starting a new run does not reset it. If the user sends an ordinary message after the approval request and the approval response arrives while that run is streaming, handlePlanApprovalResponse proceeds: sets permissionMode to bypassPermissions/prePlanMode, injects the exit reminder, then calls handleUserMessage("Execute this plan:…"), which returns silently on its this.streaming guard. Result: a mode flip to YOLO with no plan run started and no feedback; the "feedback" choice path has the same silent-drop window. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively; severity raised low->medium — planApprovalPending has no timeout and is never invalidated; an approval arriving while another run streams passes the guard, flips permissionMode mid-run, and handleUserMessage("Execute this plan: ...") is silently dropped by the streaming guard. Multi-tab use is supported (all frames broadcast), so the unbounded open-dialog window is reachable.

defect.summary: handleResume never broadcasts the new session id, leaving clients with the stale pre-resume session.
defect.detail: restoreRemoteSession replaces handle.sessionId with the resumed session, and the /clear path broadcasts a fresh connected message carrying the new session id, but the /resume path broadcasts only clear, replay messages, a system summary, and command_done. The frontend stores the session id exclusively from the connected message (fe use-chat.ts:130-133) and displays it on the welcome card (welcome.tsx:52), so state.session stays at the pre-resume id. Impact is bounded: the welcome card renders only while the chat is empty, so the stale id is visible mainly after resuming an empty session; the state field is stale regardless for any consumer.

defect.summary: TOCTOU between the duplicate-name check and team.spawnTeammate lets two parallel worktree-isolated Agent calls orphan a teammate
defect.detail: AgentTool has category "read" and no isConcurrencySafe, so partitionToolCalls (agent/index.ts:945-948) batches parallel Agent calls concurrently. In runAsTeammate, the team.getMember(requestedName) check at 448 is separated from team.spawnTeammate at 516 by await createAgentWorktree (493) when isolation="worktree", so two parallel calls with the same name can both pass the check. Team.addMember (teams/index.ts:175-180) unconditionally overwrites the Map entry, orphaning the first member: its in-process loop or external pane keeps polling the same mailbox file and consuming messages, but stopMember/stopAll only see the second entry and its cancel handle/paneId is lost. Without worktree isolation the check-to-spawn path is fully synchronous and safe.

defect.summary: External teammate exits on a shutdown_request without shutdown_response or any leader notification, leaving leader state stuck at "running"
defect.detail: teammate.ts receiving a shutdown request logs and breaks polling (390-393), then exits without sending a shutdown_response or an "[idle] … stopped" message to the leader mailbox. The SendMessageTool schema (teams/tools.ts:230-234) explicitly promises "it replies with shutdown_response"; the in-process loop acks typed requests (teams/index.ts:488-497) but the external path never does. drainLeaderMailbox (which reacts only to "[idle]" messages) never updates the member: uiState stays "running", member.active stays true, and the name stays registered, so subsequent SendMessage calls to the dead teammate vanish silently until someone manually runs TaskStop.

defect.summary: AgentDefinition fields omitMarkdown, skills, memory, and mcpServers are never parsed or consumed anywhere
defect.detail: loader.ts's YamlFrontmatterSchema (92-103) parses none of omit_markdown/skills/memory/mcp_servers, and parseAgentDefinition never sets these fields; a repo-wide search of src/ finds no reader of definition.omitMarkdown, definition.skills, definition.memory, or definition.mcpServers (spawn.ts and prompt/delegation.ts:26-35 use only name, description, initialPrompt, model, tools, disallowedTools, systemPromptOverride, maxTurns, permissionMode, background, isolation). Under the project's zero-dead-code rule these interface fields should be removed or wired up; uncertain only because they may be intentional forward API surface. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — omitMarkdown/skills/memory/mcpServers have zero readers repo-wide and the loader frontmatter schema parses none of them (the adjacent initialPrompt IS consumed via prompt/delegation.ts). Dead under the project's zero-dead-code policy; recorded, not removed (comments-only audit).

defect.summary: loadSession's mtime refresh is not wrapped, so an externally deleted session file turns a successful read into a thrown error
defect.detail: Inside the lock callback, utimesSync(filePath, now, now) runs after all lines are parsed, with no try/catch. The file lock prevents cooperative deletion (cleanExpiredSessions takes the same lock before unlinking), but a non-cooperating deletion (user rm, another tool) between the existsSync check (272) and the utimesSync makes loadSession throw ENOENT and discard the already-parsed messages. The sibling touchSession wraps the identical call in try/catch ("best-effort — the session may not exist (yet)"), showing the failure mode is known; loadSession lacks the same guard. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — the sibling touchSession wraps the identical utimesSync in try/catch ("best-effort — the session may not exist (yet)"), proving the failure mode is known; loadSession lacks the same guard, so a non-cooperating deletion between existsSync and the refresh throws ENOENT and discards the parsed messages.

defect.summary: The raw-import esbuild plugin and the matching `*?raw` ambient declaration in shims.d.ts are unused: no `?raw` import exists anywhere in src/ or tests/
defect.detail: rawImportPlugin (tsup.config.ts:124-136) is registered in both cliConfig.esbuildPlugins and libConfig.esbuildPlugins to mirror Vite-style `?raw` imports, and shims.d.ts:23 declares the `*?raw` module type. A project-wide search for `?raw` across src/ (including src/remote/fe/src) and tests/ finds zero import sites, and vitest supports `?raw` natively without the plugin. Per the repo rule "NEVER maintain dead code... Remove them aggressively", the plugin, its two registrations, and the shim declaration are removable; marked uncertain because it may be kept deliberately as contributor convenience. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — a project-wide grep across src/ (including src/remote/fe) and tests/ finds zero `?raw` import sites; vitest supports ?raw natively. The plugin (both registrations) and the shims.d.ts ambient declaration are removable dead code under the repo's zero-dead-code rule.

defect.summary: globalIgnores lists "app" and "out" directories that do not exist in apps/yukino
defect.detail: eslint.config.js globalIgnores (35-43) ignores "app" and "out" alongside real paths (dist, node_modules, and the three root config files). Neither apps/yukino/app nor apps/yukino/out exists, and no script generates them; the entries appear to be template leftovers. Harmless but stale configuration. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — neither apps/yukino/app nor apps/yukino/out exists and no package.json script generates either; both globalIgnores entries are template leftovers.

defect.summary: Temp dirs leak into the OS tmpdir in several more test files not covered by the recorded leak defect
defect.detail: Beyond the recorded at-expand/bash-background/clipboard-image/command-loader/consolidation leak, these files also mkdtempSync without rmSync: harness-data.test.ts (workDir factory line 76 + inline workDir() calls), harness-boundaries.test.ts (fixture workDir 57, "outside" dir 206), file-history-rewind.test.ts (makeTempProject 47), file-mailbox.test.ts (per-test mkdtempSync 41,54,72,84,96,108,126,146), history.test.ts (33,52,65), install-skill.test.ts (47,75,86), coordinator.test.ts (per-test workDir 67). Each run leaves dozens of directories in the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: Fake HOME temp dir created in beforeEach is never removed
defect.detail: beforeEach creates mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-home-")) and points HOME/USERPROFILE at it; afterEach restores the env vars but never rmSync's the temp home directory, leaking one directory per test. The env-restore logic shows the cleanup intent, so the missing directory removal is an oversight rather than design.

defect.summary: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var is deleted only after the assertion, leaking on failure
defect.detail: "falls back to env var" sets process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "sk-from-env", asserts resolveAPIKey, and deletes the variable only after the expect. If the expectation fails, the delete never runs and the key leaks into every later test in the process. vi.stubEnv with afterEach-style restoration would make the cleanup failure-proof.

defect.summary: Every test creates mkdtempSync work dirs that are never removed
defect.detail: Nine tests call mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-mem-"/"yukino-malformed-"/"yukino-cap-")) (first at line 83) and write memory files into them, but the file has no afterEach/afterAll rmSync. Sibling files (search-tools, shell-background, skills2, session-recovery-boundaries, prompt-contracts) all clean up, so the convention exists; this file leaks multiple directories per run.

defect.summary: makeTmpDir()/makeCheckerWithTiers temp directories are never removed
defect.detail: makeTmpDir() (line 36) is called by nearly every test, and makeCheckerWithTiers creates two more dirs per call (home + workDir), each with a written .yukino/permissions.yaml; no rmSync exists anywhere in the file. Every run leaks a dozen+ directories with rule files into the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: Mocked-home and per-test temp directories are never removed
defect.detail: beforeEach (line 63) points mocked os.homedir() at a fresh mkdtempSync dir containing a real config.yaml, and two more tests mkdtemp "yukino-defaults-"/"yukino-invalid-thinking-" dirs (301, 315); there is no afterEach/rmSync, so every run leaks directories with written config files into the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: makeRepo git-init temp directories are never removed
defect.detail: makeRepo() (line 33) runs mkdtempSync plus git init per call and both tests call it (the second creates a nested tree), but nothing ever removes these directories, leaking git-initialized temp dirs on every run.

defect.summary: Plan test work dir is never removed
defect.detail: Line 51 creates mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-plan-")) and the test writes a plan file under it; no cleanup exists. Additionally resetPlanPath() mutates module-level global state (only reset at the start of that test), which persists across the rest of the run.

defect.summary: ctx() creates a fresh work dir per test that is never removed
defect.detail: Every one of the five tests calls ctx() which runs mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-rf-img-")) and writes image/text fixture files into it; there is no afterEach/afterAll rmSync, so five directories per run accumulate in the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: makeContext() work dirs are never removed
defect.detail: makeContext() (line 59) creates a fresh mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-ps-bg-")) for each of the seven tests (each spawning real pwsh processes with that cwd), and nothing removes them; directories leak on every run on platforms where pwsh is available.

defect.summary: Per-test home and work temp dirs are never removed, including the multi-hundred-KB configs from the atomic-config test
defect.detail: beforeEach (46-53) mkdtemps a fake HOME per test and workDir() (69) mkdtemps a project dir per call; afterEach (55-67) only restores env vars and never rmSync's either. Twelve tests each leave a home dir (with .yukino/teams contents) plus one or more work dirs. The atomic-config test (305) persists a ~256 KB description and leaves the final config plus its reader-stop file on disk. The sibling pattern in teammate-mode.test.ts (rmSync in afterEach) shows cleanup is the project norm.

defect.summary: Every test mkdtemps a work dir holding spill files (up to 250 KB) that is never deleted
defect.detail: Each of the eleven tests creates mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-tr-")) and applyBudget/persistLargeResult write spill files into .yukino/sessions/s/tool-results/ (the "spills rich text" test writes a 250 KB file); no afterEach exists, so all directories persist in the OS tmpdir. The identical pattern exists in tests/tool-result-wiring.test.ts (yukino-wire-/yukino-wire-img- dirs, lines 129,178,205,231,261,341), and smaller instances of the same leak appear in tests/todo.test.ts, tests/teams.test.ts, tests/teams-shared-task.test.ts, tests/team-protocol.test.ts, and tests/teammate-registry.test.ts.

defect.summary: "lists the available tools" only asserts one of the two registered candidates
defect.detail: The test registers mcp__linear__create_issue and mcp__jira__create_issue, dispatches with server "nope", and asserts the error output contains only "mcp__linear__create_issue". The implementation joins all available names (src/tools/mcp-call.ts:280), but if a regression dropped the second candidate from the listing, the test would still pass despite the title claiming the tools (plural) are listed. Second-pass 2026-09-30: resolved definitively — the implementation joins ALL available names (src/tools/mcp-call.ts:256-262), but the test asserts only one candidate in the error output; a regression dropping the second candidate from the listing would still pass despite the plural title.

defect.summary: `expect(level).toBe("high")` asserts against a const binding that can never change, so the assertion is vacuous
defect.detail: In "does not save after a runtime setter failure" (118), level is declared const ThinkingLevel = "high" and the throwing setThinkingLevel cannot mutate it, so the final expect passes unconditionally no matter what the handler does. The same assertion is meaningful in the clamp test at 141, where level is let and the setter reassigns it. The test's other assertions (persistThinkingLevel not called, output text) still cover the contract, so impact is cosmetic, but the assertion as written cannot detect any regression.

defect.summary: plan_mode_required is silently a no-op for tmux/iTerm teammates: external teammates always run with acceptEdits while the tool result still claims "starting in plan mode".
defect.detail: Team.spawnTeammate passes the plan checker only to spawnInProcess (index.ts:266-268); spawnExternal has no checker parameter and no plan-related CLI flag is added to the spawn args (index.ts:316-336). teammate.ts hard-codes new PermissionChecker(workDir, "acceptEdits") (teammate.ts:305) and has no plan-approval mailbox loop, so the read-only-until-approved gate (runPlanApproval, index.ts:554-600) exists only in-process. agent-tool.ts:505-508 reports ", starting in plan mode" regardless of backend — the model believes edits are gated when they are not.

defect.summary: In-process teammates spawned via the SpawnTeammate tool run on the leader's registry filtered only by filterToolsForAgent: they keep leader-only team lifecycle tools, send messages as "leader", and lack the shared task-board tools their own prompt mandates.
defect.detail: SpawnTeammateTool calls t.spawnTeammate(name, task, this.runAgent) (tools.ts:152); the injected runAgent is app.tsx's teamRunAgent (ui/app.tsx:799-812, wired at :842), which runs spawnSubagent with registryRef.current. filterToolsForAgent strips SUBAGENT_DISALLOWED_TOOLS but not TEAMMATE_DISALLOWED_TOOLS (spawn.ts:94-101), so the teammate keeps TeamCreate/TeamDelete/SpawnTeammate/ListTeams, and the inherited SendMessageTool was constructed with the default senderName=LEADER_NAME (ui/app.tsx:844-846) — the teammate impersonates the leader. No TeamTask* tools are injected, yet buildTeammatePrompt instructs "Use the shared task board to record progress" (prompt/delegation.ts:22). The Agent team_name path does this correctly via cloneRegistryForTeammate + named SendMessage + task tools (agent-tool.ts:443-457).

defect.summary: The /resume handler rebuilds the conversation (dropping the MCP-instructions reminder) without ever calling syncMcpInstructions, so a resumed session runs without MCP server instructions until an unrelated connect/retry pass happens.
defect.detail: The contract in src/mcp/instructions.ts:10-15 states "/clear, /resume and compaction all drop the reminder, and once the marker is gone from history nothing is announced any more, so everything has to go out again", and syncMcpInstructions self-heals the announced set when the marker is missing (instructions.ts:47-49) — but only when invoked. app.tsx invokes it from /clear (:1561, with a comment explaining exactly this) and from applyMcpResult after connect passes (:615, :671); the /resume branch (:1692-1774) resets and rebuilds conversationRef and clears announcedSkillsRef (:1753) for the analogous skills case, but never re-syncs MCP and never clears announcedMcpServersRef. If all servers stay connected after resume, the model permanently lacks the servers' advertised instructions (aggravated when tools are deferred under mcpLoadingMode). Re-checked today: grep for syncMcpInstructions call sites in app.tsx returns exactly :615, :671, :1561 — none inside the resume case (:1692).

defect.summary: waitForNextPromptOrShutdown consumes the whole mailbox batch; when any message is a shutdown request, the other messages in the batch are dropped after being marked read.
defect.detail: receiveSync marks every message read and returns the batch (file-mailbox.ts:131-143); index.ts:527-529 returns only the shutdown message and discards the rest without requeue — the in-process twin of the recorded teammate.ts:370 message-loss defect. runPlanApproval (index.ts:571-589) shows the correct hold-and-requeue pattern in the same file.

defect.summary: A task containing raw newlines makes the iTerm osascript invocation a syntax error, so Team.spawnTeammate silently falls back to in-process and the iTerm backend never launches for multi-line tasks.
defect.detail: writeText embeds the shell command in an AppleScript string literal after escaping only backslashes and double quotes (backend.ts:122-124); raw newlines are not escaped for AppleScript, and an AppleScript string literal cannot span lines, so the `write text "..."` line (backend.ts:129) fails to compile. osascript exits non-zero, execSync throws, and the catch in Team.spawnTeammate (index.ts:270-275) degrades to spawnInProcess with no diagnostic. The tmux branch is unaffected (sh -c preserves newlines inside double quotes). Typical multi-line assignments therefore never get an iTerm pane.

defect.summary: cancelTmuxSession interpolates a disk-persisted paneId into a double-quoted shell string; a tampered config.json paneId containing ", $() or backticks executes commands in the leader's shell on stop/cancel.
defect.detail: restoreTeammateCancel builds the cancel closure from entry.paneId read out of config.json (backend.ts:80-90, team-file.ts:34, hydrated at index.ts:170); the value flows unvalidated into execSync(`tmux kill-session -t "${sessionName}"`) (backend.ts:68-72). Yukino-generated session names are safe, but the restored value comes from disk with no charset validation — the same double-quote weakness as the recorded new-session injection at backend.ts:107.

defect.summary: MemoryConsolidator.maybeRun is documented to run "when each agent loop completes" but is wired only in remote mode; terminal sessions never consolidate memories.
defect.detail: The only instantiation and call site is src/remote/server.ts:467,476. The TUI (src/ui/app.tsx) imports MemoryExtractor but never MemoryConsolidator (grep: no reference outside remote/server.ts and the module itself), so the documented automatic time+session-gated consolidation is unreachable in the primary interactive mode. Either the TUI wiring is missing or the JSDoc contract overstates where the pass runs.

defect.summary: The prompt-type slash-command turn never clears the previous `error` state, unlike runAgentTurn (2391), leaving a stale error banner through and after a successful custom-command turn.
defect.detail: The cmd.type === "prompt" branch (:1965) runs its own turn (setIsStreaming(true) then runAgentLoopWithStats then setIsStreaming(false)) without setError(null). A prior failed turn's error persists, so the banner (2875-2879) stays rendered and composer inputState remains "error" (3050-3054) even after the custom command's turn succeeds; the state only clears when a later runAgentTurn starts. The branch's catch also overwrites error without ever clearing the old one on success. Re-checked today: grep for setError(null) in app.tsx finds exactly one call site, :2391 in runAgentTurn.

defect.summary: The /rewind messageIndex fallback filters role !== "system", but ConversationManager never stores role "system" records — every reminder is role "user" — so the fallback transcript renders all injected system-reminders (long-term memory, skills, MCP instructions, plan-mode) as raw-XML user bubbles.
defect.detail: When a snapshot lacks sessionLineCount or the session file is gone (snapshots persisted by older builds are reloaded per session — see app.tsx:1762-1767 — and sessionLineCount() itself can return undefined, session/index.ts:192), rewindConversation falls back to truncateTo(snap.messageIndex) and maps getMessages().filter(m => m.role !== "system") through transcriptFromRestored (:2535-2538). Reminders are stored as role "user" (conversation/index.ts:113-118) and no code path ever adds role "system" records, so the filter is a no-op built on a wrong premise; transcriptFromRestored (1302-1363) then emits every non-empty text record as a user message, dumping raw <system-reminder> walls into the visible transcript. The sessionLineCount-based primary path (:2526-2533) is unaffected because the session log never persists reminders.

defect.summary: ToolDisplay is exported but has zero importers anywhere in src/ or tests/ (grep finds only the definition).
defect.detail: ToolCard (used by chat.tsx TurnSummaryBlock) and ToolBlock (used by agent-tool-progress.tsx) are live, but the ToolDisplay list wrapper duplicates AgentToolProgress's tools.map rendering and is imported by no module or test. AGENTS.md requires aggressive dead-code removal; recorded rather than removed because this audit is comments-only.

defect.summary: ChatView's `messages` prop is dead: the sole call site hardcodes messages={[]} and no test imports ChatView.
defect.detail: app.tsx:2858-2863 renders ChatView only for streamingText/thinkingText (committed history goes through Transcript then Static then CommittedMessage). The messages prop and its MessageBlock map (chat.tsx:59-61) can never receive data, so the prop, its ChatViewProps field (:37), and the map branch are a dead interface surface left over from the pre-Static rendering design.

defect.summary: Color-scheme query writes "\x1b[?996n" but the parser and TerminalInput only recognize "\x1b[?997;" responses, so the color-scheme detection path likely never receives a parseable reply.
defect.detail: detectTerminalTheme sends "\x1b[?996n\x1b]11;?\x07" (terminal-theme.ts:169), yet parseTerminalColorSchemeReport expects /\x1b\[\?997;(1|2)n/ (terminal-theme.ts:24) and TerminalInput only treats buffers starting with COLOR_SCHEME = "\x1b[?997;" as reports (terminal-input.ts:5). The known dark/light color-scheme protocol (Ghostty/kitty) uses 997 for both request and response; a terminal answering "\x1b[?996;…n" would neither match the parser nor be retained by TerminalInput (its bytes would flush as garbage input). Tests only cover parsing "?997;…n" (tests/terminal-theme.test.ts:46-47, tests/terminal-input.test.ts:42), not the query. Marked uncertain because terminal behavior cannot be verified from the repo, but the 996/997 asymmetry reads as a typo that silently degrades detection to the OSC-11/dark fallback. Leader resolution: uncertain resolved to false — the repo evidence alone decides it: the query writes \x1b[?996n while the parser (terminal-theme.ts:24) and the TerminalInput retention prefix (terminal-input.ts:5) only recognize ?997 responses, so the written query cannot elicit a parseable reply; color-scheme detection degrades to the OSC-11/dark fallback.

defect.summary: When the teammate shown in the detail view leaves the list, rendering falls back to the team list but key handling stays in detail mode, swallowing navigation until Escape is pressed.
defect.detail: detail = teammates.find(name === detailName) (teams-dialog.tsx:22-24); when the teammate finishes/vanishes, detail becomes undefined and the component renders the list (line 57), but useInput still enters the detail branch because detailName is non-null (lines 27-36): up/down/Enter/k/s are all swallowed by the early return, and the first Escape/left-arrow merely clears detailName (returns to "list mode") instead of closing the dialog. detailName is only reset by that explicit Escape, so list navigation is dead for one keypress after any teammate departure.

defect.summary: Tab inserts a literal "\t" into the plan-approval feedback text; the field has no key.tab guard.
defect.detail: While cursor === 2, any chunk matching `input && !key.ctrl && !key.meta` is appended verbatim (line 48-50). Ink delivers Tab as input "\t" with key.tab=true; the only tab branch (line 44) fires for Shift+Tab with non-empty feedback, so a plain Tab (and Shift+Tab on empty feedback) appends a raw tab character to feedbackText, which is then rendered (terminal tab stops) and submitted to the agent. Sibling components treat Tab as non-insertable: TextField ignores it (text-field.tsx:130-133) and updateSelectorQuery filters key.tab (selector-search.ts:20).

defect.summary: Feedback input lacks the SGR mouse-event filter that every other text-accepting surface in this scope has; a mouse report could be appended to feedbackText.
defect.detail: text-field.tsx:113-116, ask-user-dialog.tsx:314-317, selector-search.ts:39 and input.tsx:535-537 all filter chunks matching /\[<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]/ before insertion, but plan-approval's append branch checks only `input && !key.ctrl && !key.meta`, so a mouse report delivered without an escape/meta prefix would be inserted as garbage text. Uncertain only because Ink's mouse-report delivery mode cannot be verified from the repo; the defensive filters in four sibling files indicate such chunks do arrive.

defect.summary: provider-login's text-insertion branch also lacks the SGR mouse-event filter used by the other text inputs.
defect.detail: The final branch `else if (input && !key.ctrl && !key.meta) insertText(input);` (provider-login.tsx:487) has no /\[<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]/ guard, unlike text-field.tsx:113-116, ask-user-dialog.tsx:314-317 and selector-search.ts:39. If a mouse report reaches useInput without the escape prefix it is inserted into the active field (name/base_url/api_key/model/…). Same uncertainty as the plan-approval instance: depends on Ink's mouse-report delivery.

defect.summary: The command dropdown is not suppressed while the input is disabled, unlike the @-file dropdown.
defect.detail: showAtDropdown includes !disabled (input.tsx:421) but showDropdown (356-361) does not. While disabled the body renders "Waiting..." (936-939), yet a draft starting with "/" still renders the COMMANDS dropdown below it (991-1045). disabled is set to providerSwitching (app.tsx:3044), so the dropdown can remain visible during a provider switch when the draft is a partial slash command; the asymmetry with showAtDropdown shows the omission is unintentional.

defect.summary: Subtitle truncation uses detail.slice(0, 160), which can split a surrogate pair and leave a lone surrogate in the rendered subtitle.
defect.detail: subtitle={detail.length > 160 ? `${detail.slice(0, 160)}…` : detail} slices by UTF-16 code unit; argsSummary/reason come from tool arguments and may contain non-BMP characters (emoji in paths/messages), so the cut can isolate a high surrogate that renders as U+FFFD. Same defect class as the recorded plan-approval.tsx:47 backspace finding; display-only.

defect.summary: `export default Renderer` is never imported anywhere; only the named `markedTerminal` export is consumed.
defect.detail: Grep for marked-terminal across src/ shows a single consumer: markdown.ts:7 imports { markedTerminal }. The Renderer class is used internally by markedTerminal(); the default export is a leftover from the upstream marked-terminal library API. Candidate for removal (comments-only audit, so recorded not removed).

defect.summary: Renderer.textLength() public method has zero callers.
isLanguageSupported() returns true for "ansi" but no ansi grammar is registered, so ansi fences are never actually highlighted.
defect.detail: GRAMMAR_MODULES (:69-128) does not include shiki's ansi grammar, so SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES (:130) lacks it. isLanguageSupported special-cases `normalized === "ansi"` (:255), so markdown.ts:105 routes ```ansi fences into highlightCode, whose codeToTokens(lang:"ansi") throws Grammar-not-found, caught at :286-288 returning undefined, falling back to plain mdCodeBlock color. Net behavior equals the unsupported path, but the support claim is false and the fallback relies on exception control flow.

defect.summary: reflowText only recognizes SGR escapes; OSC-8 hyperlink sequences emitted by link() are measured as visible text and can be split on spaces inside the href, corrupting the hyperlink.
defect.detail: link() (:355) emits ansiEscapes.link (ESC]8;;URL BEL) at :378 when supportsHyperlinks.stdout; href.replace(/\+/g, "%20") leaves raw spaces intact (possible via markdown's <destination with space> syntax). reflowText splits fragments with /(\x1b\[(?:\d{1,3})(?:;\d{1,3})*m)/g (:527), which matches only SGR, then splits fragments on /[ \t\n]+/ (:548) — a space inside the OSC-8 sequence splits it mid-sequence. Additionally ANSI_REGEXP = ansiRegex() (:54) does not match OSC-8, so textLength (:513) counts the escape bytes toward column width. Live path: markdown.ts:69 enables reflowText. Rare (spaces in hrefs are uncommon), hence uncertain.

defect.summary: The "commands" frame is sent once per connection; ensureAgent never resends it after lazy init succeeds.
defect.detail: A client that connects while agentHandle is null receives the default registry's command list (:2340-2353 fallback). run()'s eager init failure leaves the handle null until the first message triggers ensureAgent, whose success path broadcasts only connected + status (:1209-1213) — never "commands" — so user-defined and skill commands are missing from autocomplete until the client reconnects.

defect.summary: Malformed plan_approval_response and code_review_start payloads are dropped without a log or client error.
defect.detail: In handleWsMessage, safeParse failure for these two types falls through silently, unlike user_message (:1116 logs "dropping malformed user_message") and unknown types (:1169 logs). Combined with the fe closing both dialogs optimistically before sending (app.tsx:81, app.tsx:97), an approval or review request can vanish without any trace on either side.

defect.summary: planApprovalPending never expires and is never re-broadcast.
defect.detail: Unlike pendingPermissions/pendingAsks (PENDING_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS), the plan-approval flag persists indefinitely. A client reload while a request is outstanding loses the dialog (fe state is gone) and the server does not re-broadcast it, so the approval never lands. Conversely, a late approval from a stale tab — arbitrarily later, after unrelated runs — still passes the :1977 guard, flips permissionMode, and starts the plan run, with no freshness check against the run that produced the plan.

defect.summary: clearConversation does not rotate fileStateCache, unlike /resume.
defect.detail: /clear resets conv, sessionId, fileHistory, taskList, recoveryState, and mcpAnnounced, but keeps the FileStateCache, so the brand-new conversation can Edit/Write files it never read — the Read-before-Edit gate (tools/file-state-cache.ts:22) passes on mtime entries recorded before the clear. restoreRemoteSession rotates the cache for /resume (session-state.ts:34), making the omission an inconsistency rather than a design choice.

defect.summary: No frame tells the fe that a permission/ask request timed out server-side.
defect.detail: When the 10-minute timer fires the server resolves deny (or empty answers) and broadcasts only a plain "system" message; the PermissionItem/AskUserItem in the fe stays unanswered (use-chat.ts:372-386), still showing buttons. Clicking later marks the item responded locally (use-chat.ts:481-489) while the server ignores the stale id (resolver already deleted, :1140-1146) — the UI can display "Permission: allow" while the run was actually denied.

defect.summary: Three @theme tokens are defined but never used anywhere in fe/src.
defect.detail: --color-input (main.css:18), --color-blue (main.css:29), and --animate-spin-slow (main.css:40) have no referencing class in any component (grep matches only the definitions). Dead code per AGENTS.md; recorded instead of removed per this audit's comments-only scope.

defect.summary: formatPermissionDesc's toolName parameter is never read.
defect.detail: The body uses only decision.reason and args.command/file_path; toolName is dead (the fe renders toolName separately from the permission_request payload, types.ts:64-68). Harmless but dead weight that lints like no-unused-vars with after-used would not catch.

defect.summary: `conv?.getMessages() ?? []` guards a non-nullish const: redundant optional chain and coalesce.
defect.detail: snapshotParentMessages closes over `conv`, declared `const conv = new ConversationManager()` at server.ts:561 — typed ConversationManager, never nullish on any path. `conv.getMessages()` suffices; dead defensive code under the project's zero-dead-code rule. No behavioral impact.

defect.summary: useAutoScroll's autoScroll/setAutoScroll return values are never consumed.
defect.detail: The only consumer (components/message-list.tsx:33) destructures just ref; no "jump to bottom" affordance exists in the app. Dead API surface; the JSDoc that referenced the missing affordance was corrected in this audit.

Production paths use addUserMessage/addAssistantFull/addToolResultsMessage (agent/index.ts:513/:573/:611/:642/:679/:768; remote/server.ts:384). Grep across src/ finds only the definitions; all call sites are in tests/. AGENTS.md mandates aggressive dead-code removal, but the package publishes a library entry point (package.json main/exports → dist/lib), so these may be deliberate public API — hence uncertain. If not intended as library surface, remove them and migrate the tests to the live API.

defect.summary: OpenAICompatClient sends `max_tokens` on Chat Completions; OpenAI's own reasoning models (o-series, gpt-5 family) reject that parameter with a 400 requiring `max_completion_tokens`.
defect.detail: params at :859-869 sets max_tokens: this.maxOutputTokens unconditionally. Pointing protocol openai-compat at OpenAI's Chat Completions endpoint with a reasoning model yields "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model" — a hard 400 that classifyOpenAIError surfaces as a generic LLMError. Third-party gateways (DeepSeek etc.) accept max_tokens, and first-party OpenAI is meant to use protocol "openai" (Responses API, max_output_tokens at :197), so whether this combination is a supported configuration could not be resolved from the code; the openai SDK's ChatCompletionCreateParamsStreaming still types max_tokens, so it compiles cleanly.

defect.summary: ComputerUseTool constructor options displayWidthPx, displayHeightPx, displayNumber and enableZoom are stored into private fields (:520-523, :533-536) that are never read anywhere in the class.
defect.detail: grep shows only the four constructor assignments; no this.enableZoom / this.display* reads exist. Screenshot sizing uses the MAX_SCREENSHOT_WIDTH/HEIGHT constants directly (:1268-1271), and zoom is always accepted by normalizeAction (:321-332) regardless of enableZoom=false. All three instantiations pass no options (bootstrap/tool-registry.ts:68, print-mode.ts:135, remote/server.ts:889). The options interface (:176-184) advertises knobs that silently do nothing.

defect.summary: extractBaseCmd splits only on "|", so for && / ; command chains the exit code of the LAST command is attributed to the FIRST token's hint table, producing wrong explanations.
defect.detail: Bash and PowerShell both surface the last command's exit status, but split("|").pop() keeps the whole chain and the first non-assignment token wins (:9-18). Example: `grep -q x f && diff a b` exiting 1 (files differ) yields the grep hint "no matches found" via exitCodeHint (:255-258), and formatFinalResult appends it to the tool output (shell-background.ts:266-269). Only piped chains are handled as the JSDoc (:1-5) claims; chained commands can misattribute hints.

defect.summary: validateSchema enforces the top-level type only for object/array/string; schemas declaring number, boolean or null pass without any check, contradicting the JSDoc's "covers top-level type" claim (comment now fixed).
defect.detail: Type checks at :95-103 branch on "object"/"array"/"string" only; expected==="number" or "boolean" falls through to the required-fields check and returns "" (pass). Additionally no in-repo call site passes a jsonSchema (app.tsx:857, teammate.ts:178, print-mode.ts:157, remote/server.ts:681), so the validator is currently unreachable in-app; it remains exported library surface via index.ts.

defect.summary: WriteFile success message counts a trailing newline as an extra line
defect.detail: content.split("\n").length reports 2 for a one-line file "a\n" (wc -l semantics say 1). The WriteFile schema description explicitly tells the model to include the trailing newline, so the reported line count is systematically +1 for newline-terminated files. Cosmetic only — the count appears solely in the success string.

defect.summary: runCommand kills only the direct child on timeout/abort; helper compiler grandchildren can be orphaned
defect.detail: fail() calls child.kill() (SIGTERM to the direct child only — no detached process group, no Windows taskkill /T), unlike the Bash/PowerShell tools which kill the whole tree. The long-running invocations this runner drives are the helper compilers: xcrun swiftc (:966-970, spawns swift-frontend) and powershell.exe Add-Type (:1004-1021, spawns the C# compiler), each with a 120s timeout. If either times out or is aborted mid-compile, the compiler grandchildren survive the parent kill. Uncertain because it requires a compile timeout/abort and the orphans are short-lived.

defect.summary: TaskUpdate skips empty-string values via truthiness checks, so description/owner can never be cleared, yet the tool still reports "Updated task #X".
defect.detail: if (subject) / if (description) / if (owner) (todo/tools.ts:226-234) ignore "" — the zod schema (todo/tools.ts:250-258) accepts empty strings, the update is silently dropped, and the success message is unchanged. Contrast team task-tools.ts:283 which uses typeof args.assignee === "string" and does allow clearing.

defect.summary: SharedTaskStore stores blocks/blocked_by verbatim and never maintains the reciprocal side, so the team board's dependency graph goes asymmetric.
defect.detail: create() copies the supplied arrays as-is (shared-task.ts:126-135) and update()'s addBlocks appends only to task.blocks, never to the target's blockedBy (shared-task.ts:181-190) — while the sibling todo TaskList maintains both directions (todo/index.ts:97-129). TaskList output "(blocked by: ...)" (task-tools.ts:204-206) and TaskGet's dependency display therefore show stale/one-sided relations unless the model manually updates both tasks.

defect.summary: FileMailbox.markAllRead() and FileMailbox.poll() have no callers anywhere in src/.
defect.detail: Grep finds only the declarations (file-mailbox.ts:174, :190). teammate.ts:361-363 explicitly rejects poll() ("A hand-rolled loop instead of mailbox.poll") because it cannot host the leader-liveness check. AGENTS.md mandates aggressive dead-code removal; recorded, not removed (comments-only scope).

defect.summary: idleReason is a let-binding that only ever holds "available"; the `(reason: ${idleReason})` interpolation is a constant.
defect.detail: Initialized to "available" (index.ts:413), re-assigned only to "available" after each send (index.ts:455); no path sets any other value — stopped/failed notifications use separate literal sends (index.ts:427-431, 484-496). Vestigial generalization point; misleading to readers who assume variable idle reasons reach the leader.

defect.summary: createIdleNotification builds a full FileMailMessage but every caller uses only .text; from/timestamp are re-derived inside mailbox.send.
defect.detail: notifyIdle passes createIdleNotification(args.memberName).text (teammate.ts:326-330); FileMailbox.send constructs its own message object from (from, text) when no structured message is given (file-mailbox.ts:117-124). The object wrapper is dead construction that obscures the actual wire format.

defect.summary: parseTeammateFlags uses sequential ifs instead of else-if, so each consumed flag VALUE is re-tested against the remaining flag conditions.
defect.detail: After `--task` consumes args[++i], control falls through to `if (args[i] === "--provider-index" ...)` with args[i] now holding the task text (teammate.ts:90-95). A task whose text equals a later flag literal (e.g. exactly "--provider-index") is re-consumed as that flag: the following argument becomes the value (Number() → NaN) and the task text is lost. else-if chaining or a single switch on the flag token eliminates the hazard.

defect.summary: isActive is kept optional "only for backward compatibility with older files" — a legacy shim AGENTS.md's zero-backward-compatibility policy says to remove.
defect.detail: Current snapshots always write isActive (index.ts:226), so the optionality serves only pre-existing config.json files; the same legacy tolerance appears in readLeaderPid's "team predates leaderPid tracking" contract (teammate.ts:125-131). Under the policy, missing fields should fail parse and the team be treated as not found. Recorded, not removed (comments-only scope).

defect.summary: renderTemplate substitutes variables sequentially, so an earlier variable's value containing a later variable's placeholder gets double-expanded.
defect.detail: renderTemplate loops Object.entries(vars) calling out.replaceAll per key. In buildMainTaskMessage (format.ts:117-133) change_files is replaced first and diffs second; a diff body containing the literal text "{{plan_guidance}}" or "{{confirmed_comments}}" (e.g. when reviewing yukino's own prompts.ts or its tests) is re-expanded by the later passes, injecting plan/confirmed-findings content inside <review_files>. Same mechanism applies to the filter (filter.ts:89-92), grouping, and relocation prompts.

defect.summary: extractCodeBlock's lazy fence match truncates a corrected snippet that itself contains a ``` line.
defect.detail: /```[^\n]*\n([\s\S]*?)```/ stops at the first inner ```. RELOCATION_USER instructs stripping diff markers, so an added line "+```" in a Markdown diff legitimately becomes a bare ``` inside the model's corrected snippet; extraction returns a truncated snippet, resolveComment fails, relocateWithLlm restores the original (:59-66) and the comment silently stays unresolved — for exactly the Markdown-heavy files most likely to need re-location. The recorded prompts.ts:273 false-positive covered only the prompt-input side; this is the response-parsing side.

defect.summary: DIFF_HEADER_RE's lazy split mis-parses unquoted paths containing a " b/" substring.
defect.detail: Git quotes header paths only for control/non-ASCII bytes (and core.quotepath=false is set on every invocation in git.ts), so spaces stay raw: `diff --git a/x b/y.ts b/x b/y.ts` splits at the FIRST " b/", yielding oldPath="x", newPath="y.ts b/x b/y.ts". The rename-from/to override (diff-parser.ts:211-217) only rescues rename diffs; new/modified files whose path contains " b/" get wrong paths in diffByPath, prompts, and comment filing. Distinct from the recorded git.ts:94 synthesizer-quoting defect.

defect.summary: renderReminder injects the full content of up to 5 recalled memory files with no size cap.
defect.detail: readFileSync(mem.path) results are concatenated verbatim into the recall reminder. The index path is capped (200 lines / 25KB, manager.ts:29-30) but recalled bodies are not: one large memory file (user-written, extractor-written, or consolidator-written) inflates the injected reminder that persists in conversation history, with no per-file or total byte guard.

defect.summary: The memory-selector LLM stream cannot be aborted; interrupts leave the request in flight.
defect.detail: findRelevantMemories calls client.stream(conversation, []) without a signal, and its signature accepts none. LLMClient.stream supports a third abortSignal argument (used by code-review/llm-call.ts:19). ui/app.tsx:2116-2138 creates the recall promise without binding the turn's controller.signal, so on user interrupt the selector request keeps running; the agent consumes recall only when already settled (agent/index.ts:783-794), so turns are not blocked, but the request is never cancelled and its tokens are wasted.

defect.summary: A restarted MCP server's changed instructions are never re-announced and its old announcement never retracted.
defect.detail: syncMcpInstructions filters added by !announced.has(serverName) and removed by !live.has(name). MCPManager.reconcile (manager.ts:108-145) disconnects and reconnects a config-changed server within one exclusive pass, so at the next sync the server is both live and still in `announced`: no delta is emitted even though its instruction text changed. After `/mcp reload` with edited server instructions, the model keeps the stale announced guidance indefinitely.

defect.summary: skillDirPaths maps over a constant single-element [".agents"] array — a remnant of removed multi-ecosystem support.
defect.detail: `[homedir(), ...workDir].flatMap((root) => [".agents"].map((ecosystem) => join(root, ecosystem, "skills")))` — the inner map always has exactly one constant element, so it is equivalent to join(root, ".agents", "skills"); the `ecosystem` parameter is vestigial. Per AGENTS.md's aggressive dead-code policy this indirection should be removed.

defect.summary: CommentCollector.add(), forPath(), and count() have no production callers.
defect.detail: runner.ts uses only all/addAll/snapshot/since/removeAt and comment-tool.ts only addAll. add() (:160) and forPath() (:172) are exercised solely by tests/code-review.test.ts:540-550; count() (:190) is unused anywhere including tests. No src consumer imports the CommentTool namespace (all import from submodules directly), so these are not live library surface.

defect.summary: -p mode installs no SIGINT/SIGTERM handling, so Ctrl+C mid-run terminates the process without any teardown, orphaning detached background shells and running teammates.
defect.detail: runPrintMode's cleanup (backgroundTaskManager.stopAll, teamManager.stopAll, MCP disconnect) lives in a finally block, and the sync sweep lives in recover.ts's process.on('exit') handler — but Node does not fire the 'exit' event when the process is terminated by an unhandled signal, and -p mode registers no signal handler. Terminal mode is unaffected (raw-mode stdin intercepts Ctrl+C), remote installs handlers via telemetry/index.ts:157-181 and ACP via acp/websocket.ts:146; print mode installs none. Detached background shells are exactly what bootstrap/exit-cleanup exists for (registered at tools/bash.ts:562), yet Ctrl+C leaves them running.

defect.summary: Hosts that run an Agent without a sessionId (print mode) spill tool results into .yukino/sessions/default/tool-results, a directory cleanExpiredSessions never sweeps.
defect.detail: spillDir maps an empty sessionId to "default" (tool-result/index.ts:19-20). print-mode.ts:255 constructs the Agent without sessionId and agent/index.ts:175 defaults it to "", yet applyBudget/persistLargeResult still spill (agent/index.ts:712, 738, 754) once results cross the thresholds. cleanExpiredSessions only sweeps directories keyed by an expired <id>.jsonl file (session/index.ts:579-610), and an empty sessionId skips session persistence entirely (agent/index.ts:1215-1218), so the "default" tool-results directory accumulates across every -p invocation forever.

defect.summary: Telemetry misconfiguration is swallowed silently: an unsupported OTEL exporter or protocol yields zero telemetry and zero diagnostics.
defect.detail: getProtocol and the exporter factories throw descriptive errors for unsupported values (providers.ts:87, 204, 242, 274), but every creation path runs inside safely() (:310-316), which catches and returns null without logging, and initializeTelemetry's catch (telemetry/index.ts:117-119) likewise falls back to the noop runtime silently. A user who explicitly configured OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL with a typo gets no traces and no indication why.

defect.summary: The trailing config object { ignores: ["dist/", "node_modules/"] } duplicates the "dist"/"node_modules" entries already in globalIgnores.
defect.detail: globalIgnores (eslint.config.js:13-21) already ignores dist and node_modules; the second config object containing only an ignores key adds the same two patterns again in flat-config form. Harmless but redundant configuration alongside the recorded "app"/"out" leftovers.

defect.summary: Unreachable `yield end;` after an unconditional `throw` in the mocked stream generator
defect.detail: In "stops retrying context errors when no compaction can be performed", config.client.stream is reassigned to an async generator whose body is `calls++; await Promise.resolve(); throw new ContextTooLongError(...); yield end;` — the yield can never execute. AGENTS.md mandates aggressive dead-code removal; recorded instead of removed because this audit is comments-only.

defect.summary: "opens the user-level memory dir for the consolidation sub-agent" asserts the allow case with a reason string the captured checker can never produce, so the assertion cannot fail.
defect.detail: The test captures the sub-agent's checker, which is a MemoryPermissionChecker (src/memory/consolidation.ts:123). Its check() fully overrides the base method (src/memory/permissions.ts:22-52) and only ever returns the reasons "Memory file update", "Background memory writes must stay in the memory directories and use .md files", "Memory task read", "Read outside the memory task's scope", or "Background memory tasks only support scoped file operations" — never "outside allowed directories" (that string comes from the base PathSandbox). Therefore `expect(allowed.reason).not.toContain("outside allowed directories")` passes even if the write is denied: dropping join(homedir(), ".yukino", "memory") from memoryRoots (src/memory/permissions.ts:16-19) — the exact regression the test title claims to pin — flips the verdict to deny with reason "Background memory writes must stay...", which also lacks the forbidden substring, and the test still passes. Asserting `allowed.effect === "allow"` (as the sibling blocked check asserts effect "deny") would catch it.
